q.s: A company that operates a game website for children must obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting personal information from users under age 13. Which federal law sets this requirement?
o: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
q.r: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act. The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) regulates how websites and online services directed to children under 13 collect and use personal information, including requiring verifiable parental consent. The Fair Credit Reporting Act governs consumer credit report information. The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act requires financial institutions to protect customer data and explain their information-sharing practices. The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) protects individuals' health information.
w: The Fair Credit Reporting Act governs consumer credit report information, not parental consent for children's data on websites.
The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act requires financial institutions to protect customer data, not game websites collecting children's information.
HIPAA protects people's health information, not the personal data that children's websites collect from users under 13.

q.pt: Identify ways that technology impacts business
q.s: Employees at Ridgeview Insurance work from their homes three days a week and connect to the company's network through the internet. This practice is known as
q.r: Telecommuting. Telecommuting is working from a location other than the business's office, usually from home, while staying connected through technology such as the internet, email, and video conferencing. Technology has made telecommuting practical for many businesses. Outsourcing is hiring an outside company to perform work. Job sharing is splitting one full-time position between two employees. Offshoring is moving work to another country.
w: Outsourcing is hiring an outside company to do work, but these are Ridgeview's own employees working from home.
Job sharing is splitting one full-time position between two people, while these employees each work from home part of the week.
Offshoring is moving work to another country, but these employees are simply working from their own homes.

q.pt: Identify ways that technology impacts business
q.s: A retailer and its suppliers send purchase orders and invoices directly between their computer systems in a standard electronic format instead of on paper. This technology is called
q.r: Electronic data interchange. Electronic data interchange (EDI) is the computer-to-computer exchange of business documents, such as purchase orders and invoices, in a standard format. EDI speeds up ordering, reduces paperwork, and cuts errors, which shows how technology improves business efficiency. Electronic funds transfer moves money between accounts electronically. Computer-aided design is used to create product drawings, and desktop publishing is used to lay out printed materials.
w: Electronic funds transfer moves money between accounts, but the retailer and suppliers are exchanging business documents like orders and invoices.
Computer-aided design is software for drawing and designing products, not for sending purchase orders and invoices between companies.
Desktop publishing is used to lay out printed materials like flyers, not to send business documents directly between computer systems.

q.pt: Explain the role of information systems
q.s: Which type of information system helps managers analyze data and test what-if scenarios when making nonroutine decisions?
q.r: Decision support system. A decision support system (DSS) combines data with analysis tools and models so managers can compare alternatives and project the results of different choices before making unusual or complex decisions. A transaction processing system records routine daily transactions, such as sales and payments. An office automation system supports everyday tasks such as word processing and email. A point-of-sale system processes sales at the register.
w: A transaction processing system records routine daily activity such as sales and payments; it is not designed to model what-if scenarios for unusual decisions.
An office automation system supports everyday tasks like email and word processing, not analyzing data to compare options for a nonroutine decision.
A point-of-sale system handles sales at the register and records what was sold; it does not give managers tools to test different decision scenarios.

q.s: Which computer component interprets and carries out program instructions and is often called the "brain" of the computer?
q.r: Central processing unit. The central processing unit (CPU) is the hardware component that processes data by interpreting and carrying out the instructions of software programs. Its speed greatly affects how fast a computer performs tasks. Random access memory (RAM) temporarily holds the programs and files currently in use. A hard disk drive stores programs and data permanently. A graphics card processes images for display on the monitor.
w: Random access memory temporarily holds programs and files in use, but it does not interpret and carry out the instructions itself.
A hard disk drive stores programs and data long term, but it does not process instructions like the computer's brain does.
A graphics card processes images for display, a specialized job, not interpreting and carrying out all program instructions.

q.s: What is the primary reason for creating folders and subfolders on a computer's operating system?
o: To increase the computer's processing speed
To protect the files from computer viruses
To organize files so they can be located quickly
To reduce the size of each file
q.r: To organize files so they can be located quickly. An operating system manages a computer's hardware, software, and files. One of its basic functions is file management, which allows users to create folders and subfolders that group related files, such as all documents for one client. A logical folder structure makes files easier to find. Folders do not speed up processing, protect against viruses, or compress files.
w: Folders only arrange where files are listed; they do not make the computer's processor work any faster.
Putting files in folders does nothing to block viruses, which requires security software and safe habits rather than file organization.
Moving a file into a folder leaves the file the same size; shrinking files is the job of compression tools, not folders.

q.pt: Describe the scope of the internet
q.s: A website address ending in .edu indicates that the site is sponsored by a(n)
q.r: Educational institution. The domain extension at the end of a web address identifies the type of organization that sponsors the site. The .edu extension is reserved for accredited educational institutions, such as colleges and universities. Government agencies use .gov, many nonprofit organizations use .org, and commercial businesses usually use .com. Knowing domain extensions helps internet users judge where information is coming from.
w: Government agency websites in the United States use the .gov ending, so .edu points to a school rather than a government office.
Many nonprofit organizations use the .org ending, while .edu is set aside for accredited educational institutions such as colleges.
Commercial businesses usually use .com, so a .edu address signals a school or university, not a company selling goods or services.

q.s: Lina wants to send a copy of an email to her supervisor without the other recipients knowing that the supervisor received it. Which email feature should she use?
q.r: Blind carbon copy (Bcc). The blind carbon copy (Bcc) feature sends a copy of a message to a recipient whose address is hidden from everyone else on the message. Bcc is also useful for protecting the privacy of recipients' email addresses. Recipients listed in the Cc field are visible to everyone. Forward sends a message that has already been received to someone new, and Reply all responds to everyone on a received message.
w: A carbon copy does send the supervisor a copy, but every recipient can see the Cc line, so the others would know she received it.
Forwarding sends a message Lina already received to someone new; it does not quietly copy her supervisor on an email she is sending to others.
Reply all answers everyone on a message Lina received and shows all the addresses, which is the opposite of hiding the supervisor's copy.

q.s: Keisha, a sales representative, enters all of her client meetings into a calendar app that reminds her 30 minutes before each appointment. Keisha is using the app primarily to
q.r: Manage her time. Digital calendars are personal information management applications that help users schedule appointments, track deadlines, and receive reminders. By keeping her schedule organized, Keisha can avoid missed or overlapping meetings and be more productive. Sales forecasts are usually prepared with spreadsheet software, invoices are kept in accounting or database programs, and presentations are designed with presentation software.
w: Sales forecasts are usually built with spreadsheet software, while Keisha uses the calendar app to schedule meetings and get reminders before them.
Invoices are kept in accounting or database programs, while Keisha's calendar app holds her meeting times and reminds her before each one.
Sales presentations are designed with presentation software, not a calendar app that schedules meetings and sends reminders.

q.s: Which type of personal information management application stores the names, phone numbers, email addresses, and notes about a worker's business associates?
q.r: Contact manager. A contact manager is a personal information management (PIM) application that functions as an electronic address book. It stores contact details along with notes, such as when a client was last called, so workers can quickly reach and follow up with people. Presentation programs create slide shows, web browsers display web pages, and desktop-publishing programs lay out documents such as brochures and newsletters.
w: A presentation program creates slide shows, not an organized list of business contacts with phone numbers and notes.
A web browser displays web pages; it is not designed to store names, phone numbers, and notes about a worker's business associates.
Desktop-publishing programs lay out documents like brochures and newsletters, not a searchable address book of business contacts.

q.s: Tomas is searching online for suppliers of recycled packaging located in Ohio. Which search entry will return only pages that contain all of his key terms?
q.r: Recycled AND packaging AND Ohio. Boolean operators tell a search engine how to combine keywords. The AND operator requires every linked term to appear on a page, which narrows the results to the most relevant pages. The OR operator broadens a search by returning pages that contain any one of the terms. The NOT operator excludes pages containing the term that follows it.
w: OR broadens a search by returning pages that have any one of the words, so Tomas would get pages missing Ohio or packaging.
NOT removes pages containing the word that follows it, so this entry would exclude the very packaging and Ohio pages Tomas wants.
This mix of OR and NOT would bring in pages with only one of the first two words and then cut out all pages mentioning Ohio.

q.s: When entering keywords into a search engine, Dana leaves out common words such as the, and, and of because they do little to narrow her results. These common words are called
q.r: Stop words. Stop words are very common words, such as articles, conjunctions, and prepositions, that appear on almost every web page and do little to narrow search results, so many search engines ignore them or give them little weight. Focusing on meaningful keywords makes a search more efficient. Meta tags are HTML codes that describe a web page. Hyperlinks connect one page to another, and domain names are the unique addresses of websites.
w: Meta tags are hidden codes in a web page that describe its content, not the common words Dana leaves out of her search.
Hyperlinks are clickable connections from one page to another, not common words like the, and, and of.
Domain names are website addresses, such as a company's .com address, not the common words that do little to narrow a search.

q.s: Which word-processing feature allows a user to automatically change every instance of "Jansen Corp." to "Jansen Inc." in a 40-page contract?
q.r: Find and replace. The find-and-replace feature searches a document for a specific word or phrase and substitutes new text for it, either one instance at a time or all at once. This saves time and reduces errors when editing long documents. Spell check identifies misspelled words. Mail merge combines a document with a list of names and addresses to create personalized letters. Track changes records edits so others can review them.
w: Spell check finds misspelled words, but 'Jansen Corp.' is spelled correctly, so it would not change the name to 'Jansen Inc.' throughout the contract.
Mail merge combines a document with a list of names and addresses to make personalized letters, not to swap one phrase for another throughout a contract.
Track changes records edits so others can review them, but it does not search for and replace every instance of a name automatically.

q.s: Which of the following is a guideline for designing effective presentation slides:
o: Use a different font style on each slide
Write the complete script on the slides
Limit each slide to a few key points
Add a sound effect to every transition
q.r: Limit each slide to a few key points. Effective slides support the speaker rather than replace the speaker. Limiting each slide to a few key points, often as short bullet points, keeps the audience focused and makes the information easy to read. Changing fonts from slide to slide looks inconsistent and unprofessional. Putting the entire script on slides causes audiences to read instead of listen, and frequent sound effects distract from the message.
w: Using a different font on each slide makes a presentation look inconsistent and unprofessional instead of clear and easy to follow.
Putting the complete script on the slides makes the audience read instead of listen, so slides end up replacing the speaker.
A sound effect on every transition distracts the audience from the message instead of helping them focus on key points.

q.s: The manager of a sporting goods store wants a list of all customers who spent more than $500 at the store during the past six months. What should the manager do in the store's database?
q.r: Run a query. A query is a request that searches a database and retrieves only the records that meet specified criteria, such as purchase amount and date range. Running a query quickly produces the exact customer list the manager needs. Inserting a field adds a new category of data to each record, and creating a table sets up a new set of records. A design template only changes appearance.
w: Inserting a new field adds a new category of data to every record, but the manager just needs to pull out customers who already meet the spending criteria.
Creating a new table sets up a new set of records, which does not search the existing data for customers who spent over $500 in six months.
A design template only changes how the database looks, so it cannot pick out the customers who spent more than $500 in the past six months.

q.s: A dog-grooming business wants to keep each client's name, address, pet's breed, and appointment history organized so that the information can be easily searched, sorted, and updated. The business should use __________ software.
q.r: Database. Database software stores large amounts of related information in an organized way so that users can quickly search, sort, update, and retrieve it. It is commonly used to maintain customer files, such as contact information and purchase or service histories. Presentation software creates slide shows. Word-processing software creates text documents, and desktop-publishing software designs printed materials such as flyers and brochures.
w: Presentation software builds slide shows, which would not let the business search, sort, and update client and pet records.
A word-processing document can hold text, but it cannot easily sort or search many client records by fields like breed or appointment date.
Desktop-publishing software designs printed pieces like flyers, not organized client files that need frequent searching and updating.

q.s: In a customer database, all of the information about one customer, such as name, phone number, and purchase history, makes up a
q.r: Record. A database is organized into records and fields. A record is the complete set of information about one person, item, or transaction, such as one customer. Each record is made up of fields, which are individual categories of data, such as last name or phone number. A query is a request to retrieve records that meet certain criteria, and a report presents selected data in a formatted layout.
w: A field is just one category of data, such as phone number, while the question describes all the information about one customer together.
A query is a request to find records that match certain criteria, not the set of information stored about one customer.
A report presents selected data in a formatted layout, while the question describes the full set of data for a single customer.

q.s: The owner of a bakery uses spreadsheet software to see how a 10% increase in the cost of flour would affect her monthly profit. This is an example of
q.r: What-if analysis. Spreadsheet software automatically recalculates formulas when a number is changed, so users can enter different values and immediately see how the change affects results such as costs and profit. This makes spreadsheets valuable for planning and forecasting. Data mining searches large data sets for hidden patterns. Mail merge creates personalized letters, and a database query retrieves records that meet set criteria.
w: Data mining digs through large stores of existing data for hidden patterns, but the owner is changing one number to see what would happen to profit.
Mail merge combines a list of names with a form letter to make personalized letters; it has nothing to do with testing how a flour price change affects profit.
A database query pulls out records that meet certain criteria, such as all orders from May, rather than recalculating profit under a new cost assumption.

q.s: In spreadsheet software, the box formed where a column and a row meet, such as B7, is called a
q.r: Cell. A spreadsheet is a grid of columns, identified by letters, and rows, identified by numbers. Each intersection of a column and a row is a cell, and its address, such as B7, tells users exactly where data or a formula is located. Fields and records are parts of a database, not a spreadsheet. A slide is a single page in a presentation program.
w: A field is a category of data in a database, not the box where a spreadsheet's column and row meet.
A record is a full set of information about one item in a database, not a single box in a spreadsheet grid like B7.
A slide is one page in a presentation program, which has nothing to do with the spreadsheet grid the question describes.

q.pt: Use an integrated business software application package
q.s: Which of the following is a characteristic of an integrated business software package:
o: It is designed to perform a single specialized task
Its programs share data and perform related functions
Each program must be purchased from a different vendor
Each program stores its data separately from the others
q.r: Its programs share data and perform related functions. An integrated software package combines several applications, such as word processing, spreadsheet, database, and accounting functions, that work together and share data. Information entered in one program can be used in another without being re-entered, which saves time and reduces errors. A program designed for a single task is stand-alone software. Integrated packages typically come from one vendor and do not keep each program's data separate.
w: A program built for one specialized task is stand-alone software, while an integrated package combines several programs that work together.
Integrated packages usually come from a single vendor so the programs are designed to work together, not from several different companies.
Keeping each program's data separate is the opposite of an integrated package, whose main feature is that programs share data.

q.pt: Use an integrated business software application package
q.s: Rosa copies a chart from her spreadsheet and inserts it into a word-processing report as a linked object. When she later changes the figures in the spreadsheet, the chart in her report will
o: update automatically to show the new figures.
stay the same until she re-creates the chart.
convert into a plain table of numbers.
be removed from the report automatically.
q.r: Update automatically to show the new figures. Integrated software packages, or suites, let their programs share data. When a chart is inserted as a linked object, the report keeps a connection to the original spreadsheet file, so changes made in the spreadsheet appear in the report without re-entering data. A chart that is simply pasted would stay the same until it was replaced. Linking does not convert a chart into a table or remove it from the report.
w: A chart that is only pasted would stay the same, but Rosa inserted a linked object, which stays connected to the spreadsheet and updates.
Linking keeps the chart as a chart tied to the spreadsheet; it does not change it into a plain table of numbers.
Changing figures in the spreadsheet updates a linked chart; it does not delete the chart from Rosa's report.

q.s: A project team with members in three different cities edits the same proposal at the same time online and leaves comments for one another in the document. The team is using
q.r: Collaborative software. Collaborative software, also called groupware, allows people in different locations to work together on shared files, communicate, and track one another's changes in real time. It helps remote teams coordinate work efficiently. Desktop-publishing software is used to lay out printed materials. An operating system manages a computer's hardware and software, and a stand-alone database is not designed for simultaneous group editing.
w: Desktop-publishing software is for laying out brochures and other printed pieces, not for letting people in different cities edit and comment on one file at once.
An operating system runs the computer's hardware and programs; it is not the tool that lets a scattered team co-edit a proposal and leave comments.
A stand-alone database stores records on one system for lookup, but it is not built for several people editing and commenting on a shared document in real time.

q.pt: Create and post basic web page
q.s: Before a business can publish its new website for the public to view, it must register a __________ and arrange for a __________.
q.r: Domain name; web host. A domain name is the unique address, such as a company's name followed by .com, that people type to find a website. A web host is a company that stores the site's files on a server connected to the internet so that visitors can reach it at any time. Search engines, cookies, browsers, firewalls, hyperlinks, and spreadsheets are not required to put a site online.
w: Search engines help people find sites and cookies store small bits of visitor data, but neither one gives a new site its address or a server to live on.
A browser is the program visitors use to view websites and a firewall blocks unwanted network traffic; neither provides the address and server space a site needs to go live.
Hyperlinks connect pages and spreadsheets organize numbers, but a business still needs its own web address and a host server before the public can reach its site.

q.pt: Create and post basic web page
q.s: Sana added several large, high-resolution photos to her store's home page. What effect will this most likely have on the web page?
o: The page will rank higher in search results
Visitors will be unable to print the page
The page's text will appear larger
The page will take longer to load
q.r: The page will take longer to load. Large graphic files require more data to be downloaded, so pages containing them take longer to appear in a visitor's browser. Slow-loading pages frustrate visitors, who may leave the site. Web designers therefore compress or resize images to keep file sizes small. Large photos do not improve search rankings, prevent printing, or change the size of a page's text.
w: Large photos do not raise a page's search ranking, and slow loading can actually hurt how visitors and search engines treat the page.
Adding big photos makes the page bigger to download, but it does not stop visitors from printing it.
Photos and text are separate, so adding high-resolution images does not make the page's text appear larger.

q.pt: Create and post basic web page
q.s: On every page of his firm's new website, Ian places a clickable "Home" button that returns visitors to the site's main page. Ian is using a
q.r: Hyperlink. A hyperlink is text or an image that, when clicked, takes the user to another location, such as another page on the same site or a different website. Linking every page back to the home page makes a site easy to navigate. Meta tags are hidden HTML codes that describe a page. A domain name is a site's address, and a pop-up ad is an advertisement that appears in a new window.
w: A meta tag is hidden code that describes a page to search engines; visitors cannot click it to return to the main page.
A domain name is the website's address, while Ian's clickable Home button is something that takes visitors to another page.
A pop-up ad is an advertisement that opens in a new window, not a navigation button that brings visitors back to the home page.

q.pt: Describe the nature of business records
q.s: Delmar Printing keeps a business record that lists, for each pay period, every employee's hours, gross wages, and tax withholdings. This record is a
q.r: Payroll register. Business records are documents that provide evidence of a business's activities and are kept for operating, legal, and tax purposes. A payroll register is a financial record that summarizes employees' hours, earnings, and deductions for each pay period. A personnel file holds one employee's job-related documents, such as applications and evaluations. A balance sheet reports assets, liabilities, and owner's equity, and a sales journal records sales transactions.
w: A personnel file holds documents about one employee, such as applications and evaluations, not every employee's hours and wages for each pay period.
A balance sheet reports a business's assets, liabilities and owner's equity, not employee hours, gross wages and tax withholdings.
A sales journal records sales transactions, while this record tracks what Delmar Printing pays its employees each pay period.

q.s: A hair salon keeps records of each client's preferred stylist, past services, and hair-color formula. What is the main benefit of maintaining these customer records?
o: The salon can avoid paying sales taxes
The salon no longer needs to schedule appointments
The salon can charge higher prices for each service
Employees can personalize service for each client
q.r: Employees can personalize service for each client. Customer records contain information about customers' identities, preferences, and purchase histories. When records are accurate and up to date, employees can recall each client's preferences and provide personalized service, which increases satisfaction and loyalty. Customer records do not affect a business's tax obligations or replace appointment scheduling, and they are not mainly a tool for raising prices, so the other options are incorrect.
w: Keeping notes on stylists and color formulas has no effect on what a salon owes in sales tax; the records exist to serve clients better.
Knowing a client's history does not replace booking appointments; the salon still has to schedule visits, it just serves clients better once they arrive.
The records help staff remember each client's preferences, which builds loyalty, but they are not mainly a way to justify charging more for a service.

q.s: For several years, a steadily growing number of consumers have ordered groceries online for home delivery. For grocery businesses, this pattern is best described as a
q.r: Long-term trend. A trend is a general direction or tendency of change that continues over time. Businesses monitor trends, such as the shift toward online grocery shopping, to identify opportunities and adjust their operations. A fad is a short-lived burst of popularity that fades quickly. A one-time event does not repeat, and a seasonal variation rises and falls at the same time each year.
w: A fad is a burst of popularity that fades quickly, but online grocery ordering has grown steadily for several years.
A one-time event happens once and does not repeat, while this pattern has continued and grown over several years.
A seasonal variation rises and falls at the same time each year, but online grocery orders have kept growing steadily.

q.pt: Monitor internal records for business information
q.s: The manager of a bookstore reviews the store's point-of-sale reports and notices that cookbook sales have doubled since spring. The manager is
q.r: Monitoring internal records. Internal records, such as sales reports, inventory records, and customer files, are generated by a business's own operations. Reviewing them regularly reveals what is selling, which helps managers make purchasing and promotion decisions. An environmental scan examines conditions outside the business. Outside sources include trade publications and government data, and a focus group is a form of primary research with consumers.
w: An environmental scan looks at conditions outside the business, such as the economy or competitors, while this manager is reading the store's own sales reports.
Point-of-sale reports are produced by the bookstore's own registers, so the manager is using internal data, not information from trade magazines or government sources.
A focus group is a guided discussion with a small group of consumers, but this manager is simply reviewing the store's existing sales reports.

q.pt: Conduct an environmental scan to obtain business information
q.s: A furniture manufacturer's environmental scan reveals that interest rates are rising, making it more expensive for consumers to finance large purchases. This finding is an example of a(n) __________ factor.
q.r: Economic. An environmental scan is the process of gathering and analyzing information about forces outside the business that may affect it. Economic factors include interest rates, inflation, unemployment, and consumer income, all of which influence buying power. Political factors involve laws and government actions. Technological factors involve new tools and processes, and sociocultural factors involve consumers' values, lifestyles, and demographics.
w: Political factors involve laws and government actions, while rising interest rates that make borrowing costlier are an economic condition.
Technological factors involve new tools and processes, but higher borrowing costs for consumers have nothing to do with technology.
Sociocultural factors involve values, lifestyles and demographics, while interest rates affect consumers' buying power, which makes them an economic factor.

q.s: A shoe store's sales for five days were $800, $950, $700, $1,200, and $850. What was the store's mean daily sales amount?
q.r: $900. The mean, or average, is found by adding all of the values and dividing by the number of values: ($800 + $950 + $700 + $1,200 + $850) / 5 = $4,500 / 5 = $900. The mean helps managers judge typical performance. $850 is the median, or middle value. $500 is the range ($1,200 - $700), and $1,125 results from dividing the total by four days instead of five.
w: $850 is the median, the middle value once the sales are put in order; the mean requires adding all five days and dividing by five.
$500 is the range, the gap between the highest day ($1,200) and the lowest day ($700), which shows spread rather than the average day.
$1,125 comes from dividing the $4,500 total by four, but there are five days of sales, so the total must be divided by five.

q.pt: Explain the principles of data analysis
q.s: An airline uses its past booking patterns to forecast how many seats are likely to sell on next month's flights. This is an example of __________ analytics.
q.r: Predictive. Predictive analytics uses historical data and statistical models to forecast what is likely to happen in the future, such as upcoming demand. Descriptive analytics summarizes what has already happened. Diagnostic analytics examines data to explain why something happened. Prescriptive analytics goes a step further than prediction by recommending a course of action, such as how to price seats to meet a goal.
w: Descriptive analytics only summarizes what has already happened, such as last month's bookings, while the airline is forecasting next month's seat sales.
Prescriptive analytics goes past forecasting to recommend an action, such as a pricing plan, but the airline is only estimating how many seats will sell.
Diagnostic analytics explains why something happened in the past, such as a drop in bookings, rather than forecasting future seat sales.

q.pt: Discuss the nature of data mining
q.s: An online retailer analyzes millions of past transactions and discovers that customers who buy hiking boots often purchase wool socks within a week. This is an example of
q.r: Data mining. Data mining is the process of analyzing large amounts of data to discover hidden patterns and relationships that turn raw data into useful information. The retailer can use this finding to recommend socks to boot buyers. Data backup creates copies of data to prevent loss. Data encryption codes data for security, and data entry is the process of inputting data into a system.
w: Data backup makes copies of data to prevent loss, but the retailer is analyzing transactions to find a buying pattern, not protecting its files.
Data encryption codes data to keep it secure, while the retailer is searching past transactions to discover that boot buyers often buy socks.
Data entry is typing or inputting data into a system, which comes before analysis and does not uncover patterns like boots leading to socks.

q.pt: Describe data mining tools and techniques
q.s: A data analyst sorts a store's customers into groups whose members share similar buying behaviors and characteristics. Which data mining technique is the analyst using?
q.r: Cluster analysis. Cluster analysis is a data mining technique that groups similar records, such as customers with comparable purchasing habits, so that businesses can target each group more effectively. Regression analysis examines how one variable changes in relation to another to make predictions. Anomaly detection identifies unusual records that differ from normal patterns, such as possible fraud. Data encryption protects data and is not an analysis technique.
w: Regression analysis looks at how one variable changes with another to make predictions, rather than sorting customers into groups of similar buyers.
Anomaly detection finds unusual records that stand out from normal patterns, such as possible fraud, rather than grouping customers who are alike.
Data encryption protects data by coding it for security; it is not an analysis technique and does not sort customers into groups.

q.s: While making smoothies, Callum knocks a cup of ice onto the floor behind the counter during a busy lunch rush. What should Callum do?
o: Finish serving the line of customers first
Push the ice under the counter with his foot
Clean up the ice right away
Leave it for the closing crew to mop
q.r: Clean up the ice right away. Spilled ice quickly melts into a slippery puddle, and slips and falls are among the most common workplace injuries. Employees who notice a spill should clean it up immediately or guard the area until it is cleaned. Waiting until the line of customers is served or leaving it for the closing crew allows coworkers to slip in the meantime. Pushing the ice under the counter only hides the hazard.
w: Serving the line first leaves melting ice on the floor where Callum or a coworker could slip during the rush, so the hazard must come first.
Pushing the ice under the counter only hides it; it will still melt into a slippery puddle where someone can fall.
Leaving the spill for the closing crew lets it melt into a slick puddle for hours, putting coworkers at risk of a fall in the meantime.

q.s: Although employers must provide a safe workplace, who is responsible for using safe work habits during each shift?
q.r: Each individual employee. Businesses must provide safe facilities, equipment, and training, but safety on the job ultimately depends on each worker's own behavior, such as lifting correctly, wearing protective equipment, and following procedures. An insurance agent sells coverage for losses but does not control daily work habits. OSHA and the fire marshal set and enforce rules but are not present to direct each employee's actions during a shift.
w: An insurance agent sells coverage for losses but is not at the job site and does not control how workers behave during a shift.
OSHA sets and enforces safety rules, but its field office staff are not there to direct each worker's habits during every shift.
The fire marshal enforces fire codes but is not present to guide each employee's daily work habits.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of following a safety precaution:
o: Propping a fire door open to improve airflow
Carrying a stack of boxes that blocks your view
Bending at the knees to lift a heavy carton
Standing on a rolling chair to reach a high shelf
q.r: Bending at the knees to lift a heavy carton. Lifting with the legs while keeping the back straight is a basic precaution that prevents back strain, a common workplace injury, and reflects good ergonomics. Propping a fire door open defeats its purpose of slowing the spread of fire and smoke. Carrying a stack that blocks your view and standing on a rolling chair both create hazards that can lead to falls and injuries.
w: Propping a fire door open defeats its purpose of slowing fire and smoke, so it breaks a safety rule instead of following one.
Carrying boxes stacked so high you cannot see ahead creates a tripping and collision hazard rather than preventing one.
Standing on a rolling chair is unstable and can easily lead to a fall, so it creates a hazard instead of being a precaution.

q.s: Kiara, a new employee at a print shop, decides to run the industrial paper cutter before receiving any training because she once watched a coworker use it. Kiara's action creates a(n)
q.r: Safety hazard. A hazard is anything with the potential to cause injury or damage, and operating machinery without proper training is a serious one because the user does not know the machine's dangers or safety features. A security breach involves unauthorized access to property or information. A quality standard is a requirement a product must meet. An insurance claim is a request for payment after a loss occurs, not the risky action itself.
w: A security breach involves unauthorized access to property or information, while Kiara's untrained use of a cutter puts her body at risk.
A quality standard is a requirement a product must meet, which has nothing to do with the injury risk of running a machine untrained.
An insurance claim is a request for payment after a loss happens; Kiara's risky action comes before any loss and could cause one.

q.s: While walking to her desk, an office employee notices that the power cord on a shared printer is frayed and has exposed wires. What should she do?
o: Wrap the exposed wires with tape herself
Keep using the printer until a new cord arrives
Report it and keep coworkers from using the printer
Mention it at next month's staff meeting
q.r: Report it and keep coworkers from using the printer. A frayed cord with exposed wires is an electrical shock and fire hazard that an office employee is not trained to repair. The safe precaution is to stop use of the equipment, warn others, and report the hazard to a supervisor or maintenance staff right away. Taping the wires herself is an unsafe makeshift repair, continuing to use the printer exposes people to shock, and waiting for next month's meeting leaves the hazard in place.
w: Taping exposed wires is a makeshift fix by someone not trained in electrical repair, and it could still leave a shock or fire hazard.
Continuing to use a printer with exposed wires puts the employee and coworkers at risk of shock or fire while waiting for a new cord.
Waiting until next month's meeting leaves a dangerous electrical hazard in place for weeks when it should be reported right away.

q.s: Why should employees follow safety precautions even when doing so takes a little extra time?
o: Precautions reduce the business's tax payments
Precautions replace the need for safety training
Precautions shift legal responsibility to employees
Accidents cause injuries and financial losses
q.r: Accidents cause injuries and financial losses. Workplace accidents harm employees and cost businesses money through medical expenses, higher insurance premiums, lost work time, damaged equipment, and possible lawsuits. A few extra seconds of caution prevents these costly losses. Precautions do not reduce a business's taxes, and they do not replace safety training, which is how employees learn which precautions to take. Following precautions also does not shift the employer's legal duty to provide a safe workplace onto employees.
w: Following safety precautions does not lower a business's taxes; the real payoff is avoiding injuries and the costs that come with them.
Precautions do not replace safety training; training is how employees learn which precautions to take in the first place.
Following precautions does not move the employer's legal duty to provide a safe workplace onto employees.

q.pt: Follow instructions for use of equipment, tools, and machinery
q.s: Leon's café just purchased a new commercial espresso machine. When should Leon read the machine's operating instructions?
o: After he has used it for a full shift
Only if the machine stops working properly
When the manufacturer's warranty is about to expire
Before he uses the machine for the first time
q.r: Before he uses the machine for the first time. The operator's manual explains safe setup, use, and care, so reading it before first use prevents injuries such as steam burns and avoids damaging the equipment. Using the machine for a full shift first, waiting until it malfunctions, or waiting until the warranty is about to expire means Leon would operate the machine without knowing its hazards or correct procedures.
w: Using the machine for a whole shift before reading the manual means Leon would work with steam and pressure without knowing the safe procedures.
Waiting until the machine malfunctions means Leon may already have used it unsafely or caused the damage the instructions would have prevented.
The warranty date has nothing to do with safe operation; Leon needs the instructions before his first use, not near the end of the coverage.

q.pt: Follow instructions for use of equipment, tools, and machinery
q.s: Before a maintenance technician clears a jam inside a conveyor belt, she shuts off its power source, locks the switch, and attaches a warning tag to it. This procedure is known as
q.r: Lockout/tagout. Lockout/tagout is a safety procedure that disables a machine's energy source and labels it during servicing so that no one can accidentally start it while someone is working inside. Preventive maintenance is scheduled upkeep done to avoid breakdowns. Quality sampling is inspecting a few items to judge a batch. Routine housekeeping is keeping work areas clean and orderly. None of these specifically prevents accidental startup.
w: Preventive maintenance is scheduled upkeep to avoid breakdowns, while this procedure is about keeping the machine from starting during a repair.
Quality sampling means inspecting a few products to judge a batch, which has nothing to do with shutting off and locking a machine's power.
Routine housekeeping is keeping work areas clean and orderly; it does not involve locking a power switch and tagging it with a warning.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of personal protective equipment (PPE):
o: Safety goggles worn while grinding metal
A fire extinguisher mounted on the wall
A first-aid kit stored in the break room
A guard rail installed along a loading dock
q.r: Safety goggles worn while grinding metal. Personal protective equipment is gear that an individual worker wears to reduce exposure to hazards, such as goggles, gloves, hard hats, and hearing protection. Wearing the required PPE is one of the most basic everyday safety precautions. A wall-mounted fire extinguisher, a first-aid kit, and a guard rail are important safety equipment, but they are shared workplace items rather than gear worn by an individual.
w: A fire extinguisher is important safety equipment, but it hangs on the wall for anyone to use rather than being gear a worker wears.
A first-aid kit helps treat injuries after they happen and is shared by everyone, so it is not protective gear worn by one worker.
A guard rail protects people from falls, but it is built into the dock rather than worn by an individual worker.

q.pt: Follow instructions for use of equipment, tools, and machinery
q.s: A power saw's manufacturer states that the blade guard must stay in place during operation. An employee who removes the guard so he can work faster is
q.r: Ignoring the tool's operating instructions. Manufacturers' instructions are written to protect users, and safety devices such as blade guards prevent serious injuries. Removing the guard violates those instructions and creates a hazard. Any time saved does not improve productivity in a meaningful way because an injury would stop work entirely. Preventive maintenance involves scheduled upkeep, and standard operating procedure would require the guard to remain in place.
w: Removing the guard might save a few seconds, but an injury would stop work entirely, so the change does not truly improve productivity.
Preventive maintenance is scheduled upkeep to keep tools working well, not taking off a safety device to speed up work.
Standard operating procedure for this saw would require the guard to stay on, so removing it breaks procedure rather than follows it.

q.pt: Describe health and safety regulations in business
q.s: Which federal agency sets and enforces workplace safety and health standards for most private employers in the United States?
q.r: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). OSHA, part of the U.S. Department of Labor, was created by the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970 to set and enforce workplace safety standards, conduct inspections, and provide training. The EEOC enforces laws against employment discrimination. The FTC protects consumers from unfair and deceptive business practices. The CPSC protects the public from unsafe consumer products rather than regulating workplace conditions.
w: The EEOC enforces laws against job discrimination, such as unfair hiring based on race or sex, not workplace safety and health standards.
The FTC protects consumers from unfair or deceptive business practices; it does not set safety rules for workplaces.
The CPSC deals with dangerous products sold to the public, such as unsafe toys, rather than safety conditions inside workplaces.

q.pt: Describe health and safety regulations in business
q.s: Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, who is required to provide a workplace free from recognized hazards that could cause death or serious harm?
q.r: The employer. The Occupational Safety and Health Act places the legal duty on employers to provide a workplace free from recognized serious hazards and to comply with OSHA standards, including training employees and supplying required protective equipment. A union may advocate for safety, the fire department enforces local fire codes, and an insurance company pays for covered losses, but none of them carries the employer's legal responsibility under the act.
w: A union may push for safer conditions, but the law places the duty to provide a hazard-free workplace on the employer, not the union.
The local fire department enforces fire codes, but it does not carry the legal duty to keep a business's workplace free of hazards.
An insurance company pays for covered losses, but the law makes the employer responsible for providing a safe workplace.

q.pt: Describe health and safety regulations in business
q.s: Before using a new floor-stripping chemical, a custodian reviews a document that explains the product's hazards, required protective gear, and first-aid measures. This document is a(n)
q.r: Safety Data Sheet. OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard requires chemical manufacturers to provide a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for hazardous chemicals, and employers must keep SDSs available to employees. The SDS describes hazards, safe handling, protective equipment, and emergency measures. An incident report records an accident after it happens. A purchase order authorizes buying goods. A product warranty is a promise about the product's performance, not safety guidance.
w: An incident report records an accident after it happens, while the custodian is reading safety guidance before using the chemical.
A purchase order authorizes buying goods; it does not explain a chemical's hazards, protective gear, or first aid.
A product warranty is a promise about how well a product will perform, not a guide to its hazards and safe handling.

q.pt: Describe health and safety regulations in business
q.s: A warehouse worker injures his back while unloading a truck. His employer's insurance pays for his medical care and part of his lost wages while he recovers. This coverage is
q.r: Workers' compensation. Workers' compensation is insurance, required by state law in nearly every state, that pays medical expenses and a portion of lost wages to employees who are injured or become ill because of their jobs. Unemployment insurance pays workers who lose their jobs through no fault of their own. Product liability insurance protects a business when its products harm customers. A fidelity bond protects a business against losses from employee dishonesty.
w: Unemployment insurance pays people who lose their jobs through no fault of their own, not workers who are hurt doing their jobs.
Product liability insurance protects a business when its products harm customers, not when an employee is injured at work.
A fidelity bond protects a business from losses caused by dishonest employees, not from the costs of a worker's injury.

q.pt: Report noncompliance with business health and safety regulations
q.s: After her manager ignored repeated complaints about emergency exits blocked by stacked inventory, Tamika filed a complaint with OSHA. Tamika is
q.r: Reporting noncompliance. Noncompliance is a failure to follow a required law or standard, and blocked emergency exits violate safety regulations. When internal reports do not get a hazard corrected, employees have the right to notify the proper agency, such as OSHA. A workers' compensation claim requests benefits after an on-the-job injury. A safety audit is a planned inspection, usually by the company. Reporting a legitimate hazard is not a breach of confidentiality.
w: A workers' compensation claim asks for benefits after an on-the-job injury, but Tamika is reporting a hazard to a government agency, not seeking benefits.
A safety audit is a planned inspection usually run by the company, while Tamika is taking an unfixed violation to an outside agency.
Reporting a real safety violation to the proper agency is a protected right, not a breach of confidentiality about private company information.

q.pt: Report noncompliance with business health and safety regulations
q.s: Two weeks after Marco reported a safety violation to OSHA, his employer cut his weekly hours in half as punishment. The employer is engaging in
q.r: Illegal retaliation. Retaliation is punishing an employee for reporting a violation, and the Occupational Safety and Health Act prohibits employers from firing, demoting, or cutting the hours of workers who report safety concerns. Progressive discipline is a series of increasing consequences for poor performance or misconduct. Corrective action addresses a genuine performance or safety problem, and reporting a violation is not one. A lawful layoff results from business conditions, not from an employee exercising a legal right.
w: Progressive discipline is a series of growing consequences for poor performance or misconduct, and reporting a safety violation is neither.
Corrective action fixes a genuine performance or safety problem, but Marco's report was a legal right, not a problem to correct.
A lawful layoff comes from business conditions, while Marco's hours were cut as punishment for reporting a violation.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of an input in a business's operations:
q.r: Employees' labor and skills. Operations transform inputs such as labor, materials, equipment, money, and information into outputs, which are the goods and services customers buy. Employees are a key input because their work is needed to produce products. Finished products shipped to stores are outputs. Customer satisfaction ratings and profits from sales are results that measure how well operations performed rather than resources that go into production.
w: Finished products shipped to stores are what operations produce, so they are outputs rather than resources that go into the process.
Customer satisfaction ratings measure how well the business performed after the fact; they are not a resource that goes into making a product.
Profits are a result of selling the outputs, not a resource that operations transform into goods or services.

q.s: A furniture company redesigns its assembly line so workers can build the same number of chairs using less time and material. The company has improved its
q.r: Efficiency. Efficiency is producing output with the least waste of time and resources, and improving it is a central goal of operations because it keeps costs low. Building the same number of chairs with less time and material is a clear efficiency gain. Distribution moves products from producer to user. Promotion communicates with customers to influence buying. Liquidity is a business's ability to convert assets to cash to pay its debts.
w: Distribution is moving products from the producer to customers, while the company changed how it builds chairs on the assembly line.
Promotion is communicating with customers to influence buying, which has nothing to do with using less time and material to build chairs.
Liquidity is how easily a business can turn assets into cash to pay debts, not how much time and material production uses.

q.pt: Explain the nature and scope of purchasing
q.s: A national hardware chain allows each regional manager to select and buy the merchandise for the stores in that region. The chain is using __________ purchasing.
q.r: Decentralized. In decentralized purchasing, buying authority is spread among individual stores, departments, or regional managers who know local customers' needs. Chains with widely spread stores often use it so that each area carries what local customers want. Centralized purchasing places buying for all units in one main office. Consignment means a vendor is paid only after goods sell. Reciprocal buying means buying from businesses that buy from you.
w: Centralized purchasing puts all buying decisions in one main office, but this chain lets each regional manager choose the merchandise.
Consignment is a payment arrangement in which the vendor is paid only after goods sell; it does not describe who in the chain makes buying decisions.
Reciprocal buying means purchasing from businesses that buy from you, which has nothing to do with giving regional managers buying authority.

q.pt: Explain the nature and scope of purchasing
q.s: A bicycle manufacturer buys steel tubing, paint, and tires to use in making its products. This is an example of __________ purchasing.
q.r: Industrial. Industrial purchasing is buying goods and services to use in producing other products or in operating a business, such as raw materials, component parts, and supplies. The bicycle maker uses the tubing, paint, and tires to build bicycles. Retail and wholesale buying obtain goods mainly for resale to others in the same form. Consumer purchasing is buying by individuals for their own personal use.
w: Retail buying is purchasing goods to resell to consumers, but the bicycle maker is buying materials to build its own products.
Wholesale buying gets goods to resell to other businesses in the same form, while the tubing, paint, and tires become parts of new bicycles.
Consumer purchasing is buying by individuals for personal use, while this is a business buying materials to make products.

q.s: A soft-drink bottling plant runs its filling lines 24 hours a day, seven days a week, to meet steady customer demand. The plant uses __________ production.
q.r: Continuous. Continuous production runs without stopping to turn out large quantities of identical products, which suits goods with steady, predictable demand such as soft drinks, paper, or gasoline. Intermittent production runs for limited periods and stops when enough is made, which suits seasonal or changing demand. Batch production makes a set quantity before switching products. Custom production makes one-of-a-kind items to each buyer's specifications.
w: Intermittent production starts and stops as needed, which fits changing demand, not a plant running nonstop all week to meet steady demand.
Custom production makes one-of-a-kind items to each buyer's specifications, while the bottling plant turns out huge amounts of identical drinks.
Batch production makes a set quantity and then switches or stops, but these filling lines run around the clock without stopping.

q.s: The ovens, mixers, and delivery vans that a bakery uses to make and deliver its bread are examples of
q.r: Capital goods. Capital goods are the tools, machines, equipment, and buildings a business uses to produce other goods and services, and they are a key capital resource in production. The bakery's ovens, mixers, and vans are used again and again to make and deliver bread. Raw materials, such as flour, become part of the product. Human resources are the workers. Natural resources are materials found in nature.
w: Raw materials, such as flour, become part of the bread itself, while ovens, mixers, and vans are used again and again to make and deliver it.
Human resources are the bakery's workers, not the equipment and vehicles it uses to produce and deliver bread.
Natural resources are materials found in nature, like water or land, not manufactured equipment such as ovens and delivery vans.

q.s: A person entered a convenience store, threatened the clerk with a weapon, and left with money from the cash register. This crime is
q.r: Robbery. Robbery is taking money or property directly from a person by using force, threats, or fear, which is why businesses train employees to stay calm and cooperate to avoid injury. Burglary is unlawfully entering a building, often after hours, to commit a crime. Shoplifting is secretly taking merchandise from a store without paying. Embezzlement is an employee misusing money or property that was entrusted to his or her care.
w: Burglary is unlawfully entering a building to commit a crime, often when no one is there, while this thief took money directly from the clerk by threat.
Shoplifting is secretly taking merchandise without paying, but this person openly threatened the clerk with a weapon to get cash.
Embezzlement is an employee stealing money or property trusted to his or her care, but this crime was committed by an outsider using a weapon.

q.s: To reduce the risk of employee theft, a restaurant has one employee count the day's cash receipts and a different employee prepare and record the bank deposit. This security precaution is called
q.r: Separation of duties. Separation of duties divides cash-handling responsibilities among two or more employees so that no single person controls a whole transaction, making internal theft harder to commit and easier to detect. Access control limits who can enter areas or use systems. Cross-training teaches employees to perform several jobs. Job enlargement adds more tasks to one employee's job, which would actually reduce the separation of duties.
w: Access control limits who can enter areas or use systems, while this restaurant splits the cash tasks between two different people.
Cross-training teaches employees to do several jobs, which is different from making sure no one person handles a whole cash transaction.
Job enlargement adds more tasks to one person's job, which would put more cash steps in one person's hands, the opposite of this precaution.

q.pt: Monitor projects and take corrective actions
q.s: Midway through a store-remodeling project, the team realizes it has added several tasks that were not in the original plan and is now behind schedule. Which corrective action would best get the project back on track?
o: Adding more features to impress the sponsor
Moving the deadline without telling stakeholders
Refocusing work on the original project scope
q.r: Refocusing work on the original project scope. Scope creep, the uncontrolled growth of project work beyond the plan, is a common reason projects fall behind. Monitoring progress reveals the problem, and refocusing on the approved scope is an appropriate corrective action. Adding more features worsens the delay. Canceling status meetings reduces the information needed to monitor the project. Moving the deadline without telling stakeholders violates transparency and damages trust.
w: Adding more features is the same kind of extra work that caused the delay, so it would push the project even further behind.
Status meetings help the team spot problems and track progress, so canceling them would make it harder to get the project back on track.
Quietly moving the deadline hides the problem from the people who depend on the project and damages trust instead of fixing the extra work.

q.pt: Monitor projects and take corrective actions
q.s: While monitoring a project, a manager compares the $12,000 actually spent so far with the $9,500 budgeted for this stage. The $2,500 difference is called a
q.r: Variance. A variance is the difference between planned and actual results, and identifying it is a key step in monitoring a project. Here, actual spending of $12,000 exceeds the $9,500 budget by $2,500, signaling that corrective action may be needed. A milestone is a significant checkpoint in the schedule. A deliverable is a specific product or result the project must produce. A dependency is a task that cannot start until another finishes.
w: A milestone is an important checkpoint in a project schedule, not the dollar gap between actual and budgeted spending.
A deliverable is a specific product or result the project must produce, not the $2,500 difference the manager found.
A dependency is a task that cannot start until another one finishes, which has nothing to do with comparing spending to the budget.

q.s: A dental office uses software that updates its count of gloves, masks, and cleaning supplies every time an item is used or received. The office is using a __________ inventory system.
q.r: Perpetual. A perpetual inventory system continuously updates stock records each time items are received or used, so the business always knows how much it has on hand. A physical inventory is an actual count of items. A periodic system updates records only at set intervals, such as at the end of each month. Consignment is an arrangement in which a business pays a supplier only for goods it sells.
w: A physical inventory is an actual hand count of items on the shelf, while this office's software updates counts automatically with every use.
A periodic system updates records only at set times, such as month's end, but this office's counts change every time an item is used or received.
Consignment is an arrangement where a business pays a supplier only for goods it sells, not a method of tracking supplies as they are used.

q.s: When a delivery of paper cups arrives, a café employee places the new cartons behind the older ones so the older cups are used first. This practice is called
q.r: Stock rotation. Stock rotation, also known as first-in, first-out, means using older supplies before newer ones, which prevents items from becoming damaged, outdated, or wasted while they sit in storage. Safety stock is extra inventory kept to cover unexpected demand or delays. A physical inventory is an actual count of the items on hand. A reorder point is the inventory level that signals it is time to place a new order.
w: Safety stock is extra inventory kept on hand for unexpected demand or delays, not the practice of placing new cartons behind older ones.
A physical inventory is an actual count of the items on hand, while the employee is arranging stock so the older cups get used first.
A reorder point is the stock level that signals it is time to order more, not how new and old cartons are arranged on the shelf.

q.s: A cashier at an electronics store sees a customer slip a pair of earbuds into a coat pocket. According to typical retail security policy, what should the cashier do?
o: Chase the customer into the parking lot
Loudly accuse the customer in front of others
Quietly notify the store's loss-prevention staff
Ignore it to avoid an uncomfortable situation
q.r: Quietly notify the store's loss-prevention staff. Security procedures direct employees to report suspected shoplifting to trained loss-prevention staff or a manager, who can handle the situation safely and legally. Chasing the customer could lead to injury, and loudly accusing someone could create a false-arrest or defamation claim if the employee is mistaken. Ignoring the theft defeats the policy's purpose of reducing the possibility of loss.
w: Chasing a suspected thief into the parking lot could get the cashier or others hurt, which is why policy leaves this to trained staff.
Publicly accusing a customer could embarrass the person and expose the store to legal claims if the cashier turns out to be mistaken.
Ignoring the theft avoids an awkward moment but lets the loss happen, which defeats the reason the store has security procedures at all.

q.s: At an office with badge-access doors, an employee holds the door open for an unfamiliar person who claims to have forgotten his ID badge. The employee has allowed
q.r: Tailgating. Tailgating occurs when an unauthorized person follows an authorized person through a secured entrance. Security policies require each person to use his or her own badge and direct employees to send visitors to reception, because unescorted strangers may steal property or information. Phishing uses fraudulent messages to trick people into revealing information. Embezzlement is misusing entrusted funds. Pilferage is stealing small amounts of goods over time.
w: Phishing uses fake messages, usually emails, to trick people into giving up information, but this stranger got in by following someone through a door.
Embezzlement is stealing money that someone was trusted to manage, not letting an unauthorized person into a secured building.
Pilferage is stealing small amounts of goods over time, while the question describes an unauthorized person slipping through a secured entrance.

q.s: In project planning, the individuals and groups who are affected by or have an interest in a project's outcome are the project's
q.r: Stakeholders. Stakeholders are anyone affected by or interested in a project, such as the sponsor, team members, employees, customers, and the community. Identifying stakeholders and their expectations early is one of the first steps in project planning. Competitors are rival businesses. Vendors supply goods or services and may be only one kind of stakeholder. Milestones are significant checkpoints on the project schedule, not people.
w: Competitors are rival businesses, and they usually are not the people affected by or invested in how a particular project turns out.
Vendors supply goods or services to the project and may be one kind of stakeholder, but the term for everyone affected is broader.
Milestones are key checkpoints on a project schedule, not the people or groups who have an interest in the project's outcome.

q.s: While planning a school fundraiser, the project leader decides which volunteers will handle ticket sales, setup, and cleanup. Which project activity is the leader performing?
q.r: Identifying and assigning resources. Project planning includes determining which people, money, materials, and equipment a project needs and assigning them to specific tasks before work begins. Matching volunteers to ticket sales, setup, and cleanup is resource assignment. Evaluating success happens after the project ends. Monitoring budget variance happens while work is underway. Closing out a project is the final phase, after all work is complete.
w: Evaluating success happens after the fundraiser is over, while the leader is matching volunteers to tasks before the work begins.
Monitoring budget variance compares actual spending to the plan while work is underway, not deciding who handles ticket sales and setup.
Closing out a project is the final step after all work is finished, but the leader is still planning who will do each job.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of evaluating a completed project's financial success:
o: Assigning tasks to each project team member
Comparing the final costs with the approved budget
Creating a timeline of upcoming project activities
Writing a statement of the project's scope
q.r: Comparing the final costs with the approved budget. Evaluating project success means judging whether the finished project met its objectives for scope, time, budget, and quality. Comparing actual costs with the approved budget shows whether the project delivered its results within financial limits. Assigning tasks, creating a timeline of upcoming activities, and writing a scope statement are planning activities completed before the work begins, not evaluation activities.
w: Assigning tasks to team members happens during planning, before the work begins, so it cannot show whether a finished project met its financial goals.
A timeline of upcoming activities looks ahead to work not yet done, while evaluating a completed project looks back at its actual results.
Writing a scope statement defines the project's work at the start, so it says nothing about whether the finished project stayed within budget.

q.s: A customer trips over a display stand in a store and appears to have injured her wrist. What should the employee who sees the accident do first?
o: Fill out the store's incident report
Rearrange the display so no one else trips
Attend to the customer and call for help
Ask the customer to sign a liability release
q.r: Attend to the customer and call for help. In any accident, the first priority is the injured person: assess the injury, provide basic first aid if trained, and get medical help when needed. An incident report should be completed afterward, while details are fresh, to document what happened. Correcting the display comes after the victim is cared for. Asking an injured person to sign a liability release is inappropriate and does not help the victim.
w: An incident report should be completed, but only after the injured customer has been cared for and help has been called.
Fixing the display prevents another trip, but the injured customer comes first; the display can be corrected after she is cared for.
Asking an injured customer to sign a liability release is inappropriate and does nothing to help her, which should be the employee's first concern.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of a clothing company's intangible asset:
o: The company's fleet of delivery trucks
q.r: The company's registered trademark. Intangible assets are valuable company resources that cannot be physically touched, such as trademarks, patents, copyrights, trade secrets, and customer lists. A trademark protects the company's brand name or logo, which customers recognize and trust. The retail building, delivery trucks, and sewing machines are tangible assets because they are physical property, even though they are also important to the business.
w: A retail building is a valuable asset, but it is physical property you can touch, so it is tangible rather than intangible.
Delivery trucks are important to the business, but they are physical equipment, which makes them tangible assets.
Industrial sewing machines are physical equipment used in production, so they are tangible assets even though the company depends on them.

q.s: Priya arrives at work with four tasks on her list. Which task should she complete first?
o: The files that must be organized by Friday
The sales report her manager needs by 10 a.m.
The email folders she wants to clean up
The industry newsletter she plans to read
q.r: The sales report her manager needs by 10 a.m. When prioritizing work, employees rank tasks by importance and urgency and complete the most critical, time-sensitive activities first. The sales report is both important and due within hours. Organizing the files is important but not due until Friday. Cleaning up email folders and reading the industry newsletter are routine tasks that can be scheduled for later in the day or week.
w: Organizing the files matters, but it is not due until Friday, so it can wait until after the report needed this morning.
Cleaning up email folders is a routine task with no deadline, so it should come after work that is both important and due soon.
Reading the industry newsletter can be useful, but it is not urgent and can be scheduled for later in the day or week.

q.s: Which document does a buyer send to a vendor to authorize a purchase and to specify the items, quantities, prices, and delivery terms ordered?
q.r: Purchase order. A purchase order (PO) is the buyer's written document that authorizes a vendor to ship goods and states exactly what is being ordered and on what terms; once accepted, it becomes a binding agreement. An invoice is the vendor's bill requesting payment. A requisition is an internal request asking the purchasing department to buy something. A packing slip lists the contents of a shipment and travels with the goods.
w: An invoice is the bill the vendor sends after the sale to request payment, not the buyer's document authorizing the purchase.
A requisition is an internal request asking the purchasing department to buy something; it is not sent to the vendor to place the order.
A packing slip travels with the shipment and lists what is inside the box, so it comes from the vendor after the order is placed.

q.s: Which of the following practices best helps a business maintain a safe work environment:
o: Inspecting work areas after accidents occur
Repairing equipment after it breaks down
Letting employees decide whether to report hazards
Keeping aisles and exits clear of clutter
q.r: Keeping aisles and exits clear of clutter. Good housekeeping, keeping work areas clean, orderly, and free of obstructions, is an ongoing practice that prevents trips, falls, and blocked exits. Maintaining a safe workplace requires preventing hazards rather than reacting to them. Inspecting work areas after accidents occur and repairing equipment after it breaks down are reactive approaches that let hazards cause harm first. Making hazard reporting optional allows dangerous conditions to go uncorrected.
w: Inspecting only after accidents is a reactive approach that waits for someone to get hurt before hazards are found.
Waiting until equipment breaks down lets the problem cause harm or delays first, while a safe workplace depends on preventing hazards.
Making hazard reporting optional means some dangers may never be reported or fixed, which works against a safe work environment.

q.s: When a tornado warning is issued, employees at a home-goods store move customers to an interior room without windows and stay there until authorities give the all-clear. This emergency procedure is called
q.r: Sheltering in place. Sheltering in place means staying inside a protected area of a building until the danger passes, which is the recommended response to tornadoes and some chemical releases. Employees should stay calm and follow the emergency action plan. Evacuating means leaving the building by planned routes, as in a fire. Lockout/tagout disables machines during maintenance. An incident review analyzes an event after it is over.
w: Evacuating means leaving the building by planned exit routes, as in a fire, while these employees keep customers inside a protected room.
Lockout/tagout is a procedure for shutting down and locking machines during maintenance, not for protecting people during a tornado.
An incident review analyzes an emergency after it is over, while the employees here are responding to a tornado as it is happening.

q.s: An employee receives an email that appears to come from the company's bank, asking her to click a link and confirm her network password. What should she do?
o: Report the email to IT without clicking the link
Click the link to check whether it is real
Reply to the sender to ask why it was sent
Forward the email to coworkers as a warning
q.r: Report the email to IT without clicking the link. The message shows signs of phishing, a fraudulent attempt to trick people into revealing passwords or other sensitive information. Legitimate organizations do not ask for passwords by email. Reporting it lets the IT staff block the sender and warn others. Clicking the link may install malware, replying confirms the address is active, and forwarding spreads the dangerous link to more people.
w: Clicking a link in a suspected phishing email is exactly what the scammer wants and could install malware or lead to a fake login page.
Replying to the sender tells the scammer the address is active and could start a conversation meant to trick her into sharing information.
Warning coworkers may be well-meant, but forwarding the email spreads the dangerous link to more people; IT should handle the warning.

q.pt: Explain information privacy, security, and confidentiality considerations in business
q.s: Which of the following is an example of personally identifiable information:
o: The store's total sales for the month
The average age of all store shoppers
The number of daily website visitors
q.r: A customer's Social Security number. Personally identifiable information (PII) is any data that can identify a specific individual, such as a name with a birth date, a Social Security number, or an account number. Businesses must keep PII confidential and secure to protect customers' privacy and avoid data breaches.
