Total monthly sales, average shopper age, and daily website visitors are summary figures that do not identify any particular person.
w: Total monthly sales is a business-wide figure that does not point to any single person, so it is not personally identifiable information.
An average age summarizes all shoppers together and cannot be used to identify any one individual customer.
A count of daily website visitors is a summary number that does not reveal who any individual visitor is.

q.pt: Explain the concept of supply chain
q.s: The supply chain activity of planning and managing the movement and storage of goods from suppliers to final customers is called
q.r: Logistics. Logistics is the part of supply chain management that plans, carries out, and controls the transportation, warehousing, and inventory handling of goods so the right products reach the right place at the right time. Promotion communicates with customers to influence buying. Forecasting predicts future demand, which helps logistics planning but does not move or store goods. Financing obtains the money a business needs to operate.
w: Promotion communicates with customers to influence buying; it does not plan how goods are moved and stored on the way to customers.
Forecasting predicts future demand, which helps with planning, but it does not itself manage the transportation and storage of goods.
Financing is getting the money a business needs to operate, not managing the movement and storage of goods through the supply chain.

q.pt: Coordinate work with that of team members
q.s: Javier cannot finish the restaurant's weekly staffing schedule until his coworker Ana sends him next week's sales forecast. This situation is an example of
q.r: Interdependence. Interdependence exists when team members rely on each other's work to complete their own tasks and reach shared goals. Javier needs Ana's forecast to schedule the right number of workers, so they must coordinate timing and communicate clearly. Micromanagement is excessively controlling an employee's work. Procrastination is needlessly delaying tasks. Competition occurs when individuals try to outperform each other rather than work together.
w: Micromanagement is a boss controlling every detail of someone's work, while Javier and Ana are coworkers who simply rely on each other's output.
Procrastination means putting tasks off for no good reason, but Javier is not stalling; he truly cannot finish without Ana's forecast.
Competition means trying to outdo others, while Javier and Ana must cooperate because his schedule depends on her forecast.

q.pt: Comply with policies and procedures for use of property and equipment
q.s: A delivery company requires its drivers to complete a vehicle inspection checklist before each route. The primary purpose of this policy is to
o: increase the number of deliveries made each hour.
reduce the amount drivers are paid each week.
shift vehicle repair costs to the drivers.
find problems before they cause breakdowns or accidents.
q.r: Find problems before they cause breakdowns or accidents. Policies for using company property and equipment protect employees and keep assets working. Pre-use inspections are a form of preventive maintenance that catches issues such as worn brakes or low tire pressure before they cause costly breakdowns or injuries. The checklist does not directly increase deliveries per hour, and it is not intended to reduce drivers' pay or shift vehicle repair costs to the drivers.
w: A pre-route inspection takes time rather than saving it, because its purpose is catching vehicle problems early, not squeezing more deliveries into each hour.
A safety checklist has nothing to do with lowering drivers' pay; it exists to catch vehicle problems before they cause harm.
The checklist is meant to catch problems like worn brakes early, not to make drivers pay for repairs to company vehicles.

q.pt: Explain the nature of overhead/operating costs
q.s: A boutique's monthly rent of $2,400 stays the same whether the store sells 100 items or 1,000 items. Rent is an example of a __________ cost.
q.r: Fixed. Fixed costs are operating expenses that stay the same regardless of the level of sales or production, such as rent, insurance, and salaries. Because the boutique's rent does not change with sales volume, it is fixed. Variable costs, such as packaging, rise and fall with volume. Direct costs can be traced to a specific product. Marginal cost is the added cost of producing one more unit.
w: A variable cost rises and falls with sales volume, but the boutique's rent stays at $2,400 whether it sells 100 items or 1,000.
A direct cost can be traced to a specific product, while rent covers the whole store and does not belong to any one item.
Marginal cost is the extra cost of producing or selling one more unit, but selling more items adds nothing to the boutique's rent.

q.pt: Explain the nature of overhead/operating costs
q.s: Which of the following is an example of a variable operating expense for an online retailer:
o: Annual insurance premium on the warehouse
Packaging materials used for each order shipped
Monthly lease payment for office space
Salary paid to the full-time office manager
q.r: Packaging materials used for each order shipped. Variable expenses change in direct proportion to the level of sales or production; the more orders the retailer ships, the more packaging it uses and pays for. The annual insurance premium, monthly lease payment, and salary of a full-time office manager are fixed expenses because they stay the same regardless of how many orders the business ships during the period.
w: The warehouse insurance premium is set for the year and stays the same no matter how many orders ship, which makes it a fixed expense.
A monthly lease payment stays the same whether the retailer ships ten orders or ten thousand, so it is fixed, not variable.
A full-time manager's salary does not change with the number of orders shipped, so it is a fixed expense.

q.pt: Explain employee's role in expense control
q.s: A print shop employee double-checks each customer's order specifications before starting a print run, which prevents wasted paper and costly reprints. This employee is contributing to
q.r: Expense control. Expense control is keeping a business's costs as low as possible without sacrificing quality, and every employee affects it through daily decisions about time, materials, and equipment. Preventing errors avoids waste and rework. Capital budgeting is planning long-term investments in assets. Price discrimination is charging different customers different prices. Revenue forecasting predicts future sales rather than controlling costs.
w: Capital budgeting is planning large long-term investments, such as new printing presses, not avoiding wasted paper on everyday orders.
Price discrimination is charging different customers different prices, which has nothing to do with checking orders to prevent waste.
Revenue forecasting predicts future sales, while this employee is cutting costs by preventing wasted paper and reprints.

q.s: While developing a project plan, a manager divides the overall project into smaller, more manageable tasks and organizes them in levels. The manager is creating a
q.r: Work breakdown structure. A work breakdown structure (WBS) is a hierarchy that breaks a project's total scope into smaller deliverables and tasks, making it easier to estimate time, cost, and resources and to assign responsibility. A Gantt chart displays tasks on a timeline after they have been identified. A status report updates stakeholders on progress during the project. A vendor scorecard rates a supplier's performance.
w: A Gantt chart places tasks on a timeline, but it comes after the project has been broken into tasks, which is what this manager is doing.
A status report updates stakeholders on progress while work is underway, not a tool for dividing the project into levels of tasks during planning.
A vendor scorecard rates how well a supplier performs, which has nothing to do with breaking a project into smaller tasks.

q.s: A team planning a trade-show booth learns that only two graphic designers are available, although the plan calls for four. This limitation is a
q.r: Resource constraint. A resource constraint is a limit on the people, money, materials, or equipment available for a project, and identifying constraints early lets the manager adjust schedules, reassign work, or find additional help. A scope statement describes the work and deliverables a project includes. A lessons-learned report records insights after a project ends. A success criterion is a standard set in advance for judging project results.
w: A scope statement describes what work and deliverables the project includes, not a shortage of designers available to do that work.
A lessons-learned report records insights after a project ends, while this team is still planning and has just hit a staffing limit.
A success criterion is a standard for judging the finished project, not a limit on how many people are available during planning.

q.pt: Describe crucial elements of a quality culture
q.s: In a company with a strong quality culture, frontline employees are given the authority to stop production when they spot a defect. This practice is known as
q.r: Empowerment. Empowerment gives employees the authority to make decisions and solve problems in their own work, which is a crucial element of a quality culture because the people closest to the work often spot problems first. Micromanagement is excessively controlling employees' work. Centralization keeps decision-making authority at the top of the organization. Outsourcing hires outside firms to perform work the company could do itself.
w: Micromanagement means a boss tightly controls every detail of employees' work, which is the opposite of trusting workers to stop production on their own.
Centralization keeps decision-making authority with top managers, while this company pushes the authority to stop production down to frontline workers.
Outsourcing means hiring an outside firm to do work, which has nothing to do with letting the company's own employees halt production for defects.

q.pt: Utilize quality control methods at work
q.s: A restaurant manager tests a new order-ticket system at one cooking station, checks whether order errors decrease, and then decides whether to adopt it at every station. The manager is using the
q.r: Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle. The Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle is a four-step quality-control method for testing a change on a small scale, measuring the results, and then adopting or adjusting it. It supports continuous improvement. The critical path method identifies the longest chain of dependent project tasks. The sealed-bid process is a purchasing method. The periodic inventory method updates stock records at set intervals.
w: The critical path method finds the longest chain of dependent tasks in a project schedule, not a way to test a change and check its results.
A sealed-bid process is a way to collect private price offers from suppliers, not a method for testing and evaluating a kitchen improvement.
The periodic inventory method updates stock counts at set intervals, which has nothing to do with testing a new order-ticket system.

q.pt: Discuss the role of ethics in operations
q.s: A production supervisor learns that a cheaper material would cut costs but would cause the company's product to wear out sooner than its advertising promises. What is the most ethical action?
o: Keep using material that meets the product's promises
Switch materials and raise the product's price
Let customers discover the change on their own
q.r: Keep using material that meets the product's promises. Ethics in operations means making production and purchasing decisions that are honest and responsible even when cutting corners would save money. Customers rely on the company's quality claims, so secretly lowering quality would deceive them. Switching materials without telling customers, raising the price for a lesser product, or letting customers discover the change all mislead buyers and risk the company's reputation.
w: Switching materials without telling customers would secretly break the product's promises, deceiving buyers who rely on the company's claims.
Raising the price while switching to a material that wears out sooner makes customers pay more for a product that no longer lives up to its promises.
Letting customers find out on their own still deceives them, since they bought the product expecting it to last as long as advertised.

q.pt: Describe the use of technology in operations
q.s: A distribution center attaches small radio tags to pallets so that readers can automatically track each pallet's location without scanning its label in a direct line of sight. This technology is
q.r: Radio frequency identification (RFID). RFID uses radio waves to read tags attached to items, allowing businesses to track inventory automatically and quickly without line-of-sight scanning. Computer-aided design software is used to design products. Enterprise resource planning software integrates core business processes in one database. A universal product code is a bar code that must be scanned in a direct line of sight to be read.
w: Computer-aided design is software for designing products, not a way to track pallets with radio tags.
Enterprise resource planning software connects a company's business processes in one system, but it is not the tag technology that reads pallets by radio.
A universal product code is a bar code that must be scanned in a direct line of sight, which is exactly what this system avoids.

q.pt: Apply project-management tools to monitor and communicate project progress
q.s: A project manager wants a visual tool that shows each task as a horizontal bar along a timeline so stakeholders can see start dates, durations, and overlapping tasks. The manager should use a
q.r: Gantt chart. A Gantt chart is a bar chart that displays project tasks against a calendar timeline, making it easy to monitor progress and communicate the schedule to stakeholders. A work breakdown structure lists and organizes tasks but does not show them on a timeline. An organizational chart shows reporting relationships among employees. A pie chart shows the parts of a whole and is not used for scheduling.
w: A work breakdown structure lists and organizes a project's tasks, but it does not show them as bars along a timeline with start dates and overlaps.
An organizational chart shows who reports to whom in a company, not tasks, dates and durations along a project timeline.
A pie chart shows how parts make up a whole, such as budget shares, and cannot show tasks, start dates or overlaps over time.

q.pt: Explain the nature of project management
q.s: Which of the following is an example of a project:
o: Opening a second store location by next June
q.r: Opening a second store location by next June. A project is a temporary effort with a defined beginning, a defined end, and a unique result. Opening a new store has a clear goal and deadline and will be finished once the store opens. Processing payments, restocking shelves, and answering customer emails are ongoing, repetitive operations that continue indefinitely rather than temporary efforts that produce a unique result.
w: Processing customer payments each day is an ongoing, repeated operation with no end date, while a project is temporary and produces a unique result.
Restocking shelves every morning is routine work that continues indefinitely, not a temporary effort with a defined end like opening a new store.
Answering customer emails every week is an ongoing operation that never finishes, so it lacks the defined end and unique result a project has.

q.s: During a job interview, Keandre is asked a long, two-part question about how he would handle an upset customer. What should Keandre do to answer the question effectively?
o: Start answering as soon as he recognizes the topic
Listen carefully to the entire question before responding
Answer only the part of the question he likes best
Ask the interviewer to skip to an easier question
q.r: Listen carefully to the entire question before responding. Listening carefully to the entire question allows an applicant to understand exactly what the interviewer wants to know and to address every part of it. Responding too soon can lead to an incomplete or off-target answer that suggests weak communication skills. Starting before the question is finished, answering only one part, and asking to skip the question all signal poor listening and preparation to the interviewer.
w: Jumping in as soon as he recognizes the topic means Keandre could miss the second part of the question and give an incomplete answer.
Answering only the part he likes best leaves the rest of the question unanswered and suggests poor listening to the interviewer.
Asking to skip the question signals that Keandre is unprepared and avoids a topic the interviewer clearly wants to know about.

q.s: To display positive body language during a job interview, an applicant should
o: lean back in the chair with arms folded.
glance at a phone between questions.
tap a pen while the interviewer talks.
sit up straight and make regular eye contact.
q.r: Sit up straight and make regular eye contact. Body language is the nonverbal message a person sends through posture, facial expressions, gestures, and eye contact. Good posture and regular eye contact show the interviewer that the applicant is confident, interested, and attentive. Folded arms can suggest defensiveness, checking a phone signals disinterest, and tapping a pen suggests nervousness or impatience.
w: Leaning back with folded arms can look closed off or uninterested, which sends the wrong message to an interviewer.
Glancing at a phone during an interview signals that the applicant is distracted and not fully interested in the conversation.
Tapping a pen while the interviewer talks suggests nervousness or impatience rather than confident attention.

q.s: An interviewer asks Priya, "Tell me about a time when you had to meet a tight deadline at work or school." This is an example of a(n) __________ question.
q.r: Behavioral. A behavioral interview question asks an applicant to describe how he or she handled a specific past situation, because past behavior helps predict future performance. Applicants can answer these questions well by using the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, and Result. A hypothetical question asks what the applicant would do in an imagined situation. An illegal question involves a protected characteristic such as age or religion. A closed-ended question can be answered with one word.
w: A hypothetical question asks what an applicant would do in an imagined situation, but Priya is asked about a time that actually happened.
An illegal question involves a protected characteristic like age or religion, and asking about meeting deadlines is a fair job-related question.
A closed-ended question can be answered with a word like yes or no, while this one asks Priya to tell a full story.

q.s: Rhea is starting a new job at an insurance office and is not yet sure what clothing her coworkers usually wear. Which of the following is the best guideline for her to follow:
o: Wear the latest fashion trends to make a strong impression
Dress the way she normally dresses on weekends
Select bright, bold colors so that customers notice her
Choose neat, conservative clothing until she learns the norms
q.r: Choose neat, conservative clothing until she learns the norms. When unsure of a workplace's standards, employees should dress conservatively, choosing clean, well-fitting, understated clothing. Conservative attire rarely offends anyone and helps create a positive first impression; once Rhea learns the dress code and what coworkers wear, she can adjust. Trendy, weekend, or eye-catching clothing may be inappropriate for a professional office and can distract others from her work.
w: The latest trends may look out of place in a professional insurance office and can draw attention away from Rhea's work.
Weekend clothing is usually too casual for a professional office, especially before Rhea knows what the dress norms are.
Bright, bold colors meant to get noticed can be distracting in an office, while the safest choice while unsure is understated clothing.

q.s: Why do many businesses require employees who work with customers to follow a dress code?
o: Dress codes make it easier for businesses to calculate wages
Employees' appearance affects customers' image of the business
Uniform clothing replaces the need for customer service training
Dress codes encourage employees to express their personal style
q.r: Employees' appearance affects customers' image of the business. Customers often judge a business by the appearance of the people who represent it. A dress code is a written policy setting standards for acceptable clothing and grooming, so employees present a consistent, professional image that builds customer confidence. Dress codes have nothing to do with calculating wages and do not replace training. They usually limit, rather than encourage, personal style at work.
w: Dress codes deal with appearance and have nothing to do with how a business figures out employees' pay.
Matching clothes cannot teach employees how to serve customers well, so a dress code does not replace training.
Dress codes usually limit personal style at work so employees present a consistent, professional image to customers.

q.s: Showering daily, using deodorant, and keeping fingernails clean and trimmed are practices that maintain good personal
q.r: Hygiene. Personal hygiene refers to the daily grooming practices that keep the body clean and healthy, such as bathing, brushing teeth, and caring for hair and nails. Poor hygiene can offend customers and coworkers and hold back an otherwise capable employee. Wardrobe refers to a person's clothing. Posture is the way a person holds his or her body. Etiquette is the set of rules for polite, courteous behavior.
w: Wardrobe means the clothes a person wears, while showering, deodorant, and nail care are about keeping the body itself clean.
Posture is how a person holds their body when sitting or standing, not daily cleanliness habits like showering and trimming nails.
Etiquette is the set of rules for polite behavior, not personal cleanliness routines like bathing and using deodorant.

q.pt: Assess personal interests and skills needed for success in business
q.s: What is the primary purpose of assessing your personal interests and skills?
o: To compare your abilities with those of your classmates
To identify careers that are a good fit for you
To determine the starting salary you should request
q.r: To identify careers that are a good fit for you. Self-assessment is the process of evaluating your own interests, skills, values, and personality. Understanding yourself helps you identify careers that match what you enjoy and do well, which increases your chances of job satisfaction and success. Self-assessment focuses on you, not on comparisons with others. It does not determine salary requests or eligibility for employee benefits.
w: Self-assessment focuses on your own interests and abilities, not on ranking yourself against classmates.
Knowing your interests and skills helps you choose a career direction; it is not a tool for deciding what salary to ask for.
Benefit eligibility is set by employer policies, not by assessing your own interests and skills.

q.pt: Assess personal interests and skills needed for success in business
q.s: Leila is skilled at using spreadsheet software and preparing financial statements, abilities she learned in her accounting classes. These abilities are examples of
q.r: Hard skills. Hard skills are teachable, job-specific abilities that can be measured, such as using spreadsheet software, preparing financial statements, or coding. Workers usually gain them through classes, training, and practice. Soft skills, such as communication and teamwork, are interpersonal traits that apply to almost any job; interpersonal skills are one type of soft skill. Personality traits are characteristics, such as being outgoing, rather than learned technical abilities.
w: Soft skills are people skills like communication and teamwork, while spreadsheet use and financial statements are specific technical abilities.
Interpersonal skills are about working well with others, but Leila's abilities are measurable technical skills learned in accounting classes.
Personality traits are natural characteristics like being outgoing, not technical abilities Leila learned in classes.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of systematic behavior at work:
o: Using a checklist to complete nightly closing duties
Completing whichever tasks seem most enjoyable at the moment
Waiting for a supervisor to explain each step of a routine task
Switching between several tasks whenever one becomes boring
q.r: Using a checklist to complete nightly closing duties. Systematic behavior means working in an orderly, planned way by organizing tasks and following established procedures. A checklist helps an employee complete every required step in a consistent order, which improves accuracy and efficiency. Choosing tasks by enjoyment or switching when bored leads to missed steps and wasted time. Relying on a supervisor for every step of a routine task shows a lack of organization and self-management.
w: Choosing tasks by what feels enjoyable is the opposite of an orderly plan, and it can leave important duties unfinished.
Needing a supervisor to explain every step of a routine task shows a lack of self-management rather than an organized, planned approach.
Jumping between tasks whenever boredom hits breaks up any planned order and makes it easy to miss steps or waste time.

q.s: Darnell plans his workday the evening before, keeps his files organized, and clears unneeded papers from his desk each week. What is the main benefit of Darnell's behavior?
o: He no longer needs to set priorities for his tasks
He can work at a steady pace and make fewer errors
He can rely on coworkers to keep track of his tasks
He reduces the need to follow company procedures
q.r: He can work at a steady pace and make fewer errors. Planning ahead and keeping an orderly workspace are habits of systematic workers. Because Darnell knows what needs to be done and can find what he needs quickly, he wastes less time and can work at a relaxed, steady pace with fewer mistakes. Being organized does not replace setting priorities or following company procedures; it supports them. Organized workers manage their own tasks rather than relying on coworkers.
w: Being organized does not remove the need to set priorities; Darnell's planning actually helps him decide what matters most each day.
Darnell's habits help him keep track of his own work, so he depends less on coworkers rather than relying on them.
Organization supports following company procedures; it does not make those procedures any less necessary.

q.pt: Describe techniques for obtaining work experience (e.g., volunteer activities, internships)
q.s: Mia wants to become a veterinarian but cannot find a paid job in the field. Which of the following would be the best way for her to gain relevant work experience:
o: Take a part-time job at a clothing store
Volunteer at a local animal shelter
Wait until after college to look for experience
Watch online videos about caring for pets
q.r: Volunteer at a local animal shelter. Volunteering is unpaid service that provides real work experience, skills, and references in a chosen field. Working with animals at a shelter gives Mia hands-on experience directly related to veterinary medicine and strengthens her resume. A clothing store job provides general work experience but is unrelated to her career goal. Waiting delays her preparation, and watching videos does not provide practical, supervised work experience.
w: A clothing store job gives general work experience, but it has nothing to do with animals or veterinary medicine, which is Mia's goal.
Waiting until after college delays experience Mia could start building now, which would strengthen her preparation and her applications.
Videos may teach her a little about pet care, but they do not give the hands-on, supervised experience that counts as real work experience.

q.pt: Describe techniques for obtaining work experience (e.g., volunteer activities, internships)
q.s: A temporary position in which a student gains supervised, practical experience in a career field, sometimes for pay and sometimes for school credit, is a(n)
q.r: Internship. An internship is a short-term work arrangement that lets students or recent graduates gain practical experience in a career field under the supervision of experienced workers. Internships build skills, professional contacts, and references. An apprenticeship is paid on-the-job training combined with instruction in a skilled trade, usually lasting several years. A franchise is a license to operate a business using another company's brand. A sabbatical is an extended break from work.
w: An apprenticeship is paid on-the-job training in a skilled trade that usually lasts several years, not a short temporary position for a student.
A franchise is a license to run a business using another company's brand, not a temporary job for gaining career experience.
A sabbatical is an extended break from work, which is the opposite of a position where a student gains hands-on experience.

q.pt: Explain the need for ongoing education as a worker
q.s: Why do many workers continue their education after they begin their careers?
o: To meet a federal law requiring yearly college classes
To reduce the number of hours they are required to work
To avoid having to learn new tasks on the job
To keep their skills current as job requirements change
q.r: To keep their skills current as job requirements change. Technology and business practices change constantly, so skills that are valuable today may become obsolete. Ongoing education, or lifelong learning, helps workers stay capable and employable and prepares them for future jobs and promotions. No federal law requires workers to take yearly college classes. Continuing education does not reduce required work hours, and it prepares workers to learn new tasks rather than avoid them.
w: No federal law requires workers to take college classes every year; people keep learning because job skills change over time.
Ongoing education is usually added on top of a job, so it does not reduce the number of hours a worker is required to work.
Continuing education helps workers handle new tasks, not avoid them, since job requirements keep changing.

q.pt: Explain the need for ongoing education as a worker
q.s: Hollister Manufacturing pays part of the cost of college courses that its employees complete with a passing grade. This employee benefit is called
q.r: Tuition assistance. Tuition assistance, sometimes called tuition reimbursement, is an employer's payment toward the cost of an employee's education. Employers offer it to encourage continuing education, which builds a more skilled workforce. Profit sharing gives employees part of the company's profits. A signing bonus is a one-time payment for accepting a job offer. Workers' compensation provides benefits to employees who are injured or become ill because of their jobs.
w: Profit sharing gives employees part of the company's profits, while Hollister is paying toward the cost of employees' college courses.
A signing bonus is a one-time payment for accepting a job offer, not ongoing help paying for college courses.
Workers' compensation pays benefits to employees hurt or made ill by their jobs, not toward the cost of college classes.

q.s: A job application asks for the phone number of Ty's former supervisor, but the business has closed and Ty cannot locate the number. What should Ty do?
o: Leave the entire work history section blank
Enter a phone number that looks realistic
List his own phone number in the space
q.r: Write "unknown" in the space provided. Applicants should answer every question on a job application completely and honestly. When information truly cannot be found, writing "unknown" (or "N/A" when a question does not apply) shows the employer that the question was not skipped by mistake. Leaving a whole section blank makes the application look incomplete. Entering a made-up or incorrect number is dishonest and could cost Ty the job if it is discovered.
w: Leaving the whole work history blank makes the application look incomplete when only one detail, the phone number, is actually missing.
Making up a phone number is dishonest, and if the employer discovers it, Ty could lose the job opportunity.
Listing his own number is incorrect information that could confuse the employer, since the space asks for the former supervisor's number.

q.pt: Analyze employer expectations in the business environment
q.s: During a slow period at work, Corinne notices several empty shelves and restocks them without being asked. Corinne is demonstrating
q.r: Initiative. Initiative is doing what needs to be done without being told, and it is one of the qualities employers value most. Employees who show initiative save managers time and contribute to the business's success. Seniority is status based on length of service with an employer. Insubordination is refusing to follow a supervisor's reasonable instructions. Dependency is relying on others for direction, which is the opposite of initiative.
w: Seniority is status earned through length of service with an employer, not the act of seeing work that needs doing and doing it.
Insubordination is refusing a supervisor's reasonable instructions, while Corinne is doing helpful work no one even asked her to do.
Dependency means relying on others for direction, which is the opposite of Corinne restocking shelves on her own.

q.s: After Jalen files a complaint with OSHA about an unsafe machine at his workplace, his supervisor cuts his weekly hours in half. The supervisor's action is an example of
q.r: Retaliation. Retaliation is punishing an employee for exercising a legal right, such as reporting a safety hazard or filing a discrimination complaint. Workers have the right to a safe workplace, and federal law protects them from retaliation for reporting hazards to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). Progressive discipline applies increasingly serious penalties for repeated policy violations. Collective bargaining is negotiation between a union and an employer. Constructive feedback is helpful criticism.
w: Progressive discipline applies stronger penalties for repeated rule violations, but Jalen broke no rule; he reported a hazard, which is his legal right.
Collective bargaining is negotiation between a union and an employer over working conditions, not a supervisor punishing one worker for a complaint.
Constructive feedback is helpful criticism meant to improve performance, not cutting someone's hours for reporting a safety problem.

q.pt: Explain possible advancement patterns for jobs
q.s: Over eight years, Simone moved from sales associate to department manager to store manager within the same retail chain. Simone's advancement followed a career
q.r: Ladder. A career ladder is a sequence of jobs leading upward from entry-level to higher positions with more responsibility and pay, often within one organization. Each promotion builds on experience gained in the previous job. A career lattice combines upward moves with lateral moves into different areas. A career cluster is a broad group of occupations sharing common knowledge and skills. A career portfolio is a collection of work samples, not an advancement pattern.
w: A career lattice mixes upward moves with sideways moves into different areas, while Simone moved straight up through higher positions.
A career cluster is a broad group of related occupations, not a pattern describing how one person moves up through jobs.
A career portfolio is a collection of work samples and accomplishments, not a description of how Simone advanced through her jobs.

q.s: Many job openings are filled through personal contacts and referrals without ever being publicly advertised. These unadvertised openings make up the
q.r: Hidden job market. The hidden job market consists of job openings filled without public advertising, often through employee referrals, professional contacts, and direct inquiries. Job seekers reach it by networking and by contacting employers directly. The secondary labor market refers to low-wage jobs with little security or chance of advancement. A public job board is a website that advertises openings from many employers. A seasonal job market includes jobs available only at certain times of the year.
w: The secondary labor market refers to low-wage jobs with little security, not to openings that are filled without being advertised.
A public job board advertises openings for everyone to see, which is the opposite of jobs filled quietly through contacts and referrals.
A seasonal job market includes jobs available only at certain times of year, not openings that are never publicly posted.

q.s: Rafael wants a business career that involves recruiting, training, and compensating a company's workers. Which career area best fits Rafael's interests?
q.r: Human resources management. Human resources management is the business function concerned with recruiting, hiring, training, compensating, and retaining employees. Careers in this area include recruiter, trainer, and compensation specialist. Marketing communications careers involve promotion, such as advertising and public relations. Financial analysis careers focus on evaluating financial data to guide money decisions. Operations management careers focus on the processes that produce goods and services.
w: Marketing communications careers focus on advertising and public relations, not on recruiting, training, and paying a company's workers.
Financial analysis careers involve studying financial data to guide money decisions, not hiring and developing employees.
Operations management deals with the processes that produce goods and services, while Rafael's interests center on managing the workforce itself.

q.s: Hospitals, schools, and nonprofit organizations all need people to manage, finance, and market their activities. This shows that employment opportunities in business
o: are found mainly in retail stores.
are concentrated in the technology sector.
q.r: Exist in nearly every industry. Every organization, whether it sells goods, provides services, or pursues a nonprofit mission, must perform business functions such as management, finance, marketing, and operations. As a result, business careers are available in virtually every industry and at every level, from entry-level jobs to top management. Business jobs are not limited to large corporations, retail stores, or the technology sector.
w: Hospitals, schools, and nonprofits are not large corporations, yet they need business workers, which shows these jobs are not limited to big companies.
The examples in the question are hospitals, schools, and nonprofits, not stores, so business jobs clearly reach well beyond retail.
None of the organizations named is a technology company, which shows business careers are spread across many industries, not just tech.

q.s: A bank teller position that requires a high school diploma but no prior work experience is an example of a(n)
q.r: Entry-level job. An entry-level job is a position that requires little or no prior work experience or training beyond basic education. Entry-level jobs give new workers a starting point in a business career, where they can build the skills and experience that lead to advancement. Supervisory and middle-management positions require experience in directing other workers, and executive positions are top-management jobs that require years of experience and broad business knowledge.
w: An executive position is a top-management job that requires years of experience, not a role that needs only a high school diploma.
Middle-management jobs require experience directing other workers, while this teller job asks for no prior work experience.
A supervisory position involves overseeing other employees and usually requires experience, unlike this teller job.

q.s: Which of the following is a characteristic shared by many successful entrepreneurs:
o: A strong preference for avoiding risk
A desire to be told exactly what to do
An unwillingness to change their plans
q.r: Persistence in working through setbacks. Entrepreneurs start and run businesses and assume the risks involved, so they face frequent obstacles. Successful entrepreneurs tend to be determined, self-confident, and persistent, continuing to work toward their goals despite difficulties. Entrepreneurs accept moderate, calculated risks rather than avoiding risk. They are usually self-directed rather than needing instructions, and they are flexible enough to adjust their plans when conditions change.
w: Entrepreneurs must accept risk to start a business, so most take on moderate, calculated risks rather than trying to avoid risk altogether.
Entrepreneurs are usually self-directed and make their own decisions, so needing to be told exactly what to do does not fit them.
Conditions change quickly for new businesses, so successful entrepreneurs tend to be flexible and willing to adjust their plans.

q.s: Dana, a product designer at a large toy company, proposes and leads the development of a new line of eco-friendly toys for her employer. Dana is acting as a(n)
q.r: Intrapreneur. An intrapreneur is an employee who thinks and acts like an entrepreneur within an existing company, developing new ideas, products, or processes for the employer. Intrapreneurship lets people use entrepreneurial skills without starting their own businesses. A franchisee buys the right to operate a business using another company's brand and system. A sole proprietor owns a business alone. A venture capitalist invests money in new businesses in exchange for ownership.
w: A franchisee buys the right to run a business under another company's brand, while Dana is an employee creating a new product line for her employer.
A sole proprietor owns a business alone, but Dana works for a large toy company rather than owning her own business.
A venture capitalist invests money in new businesses in exchange for ownership, while Dana is leading product development inside her own company.

q.s: One of the most common reasons new businesses fail is insufficient capital, which means that the owner
o: does not have enough employees to serve customers.
does not offer enough products to attract customers.
does not have enough money to operate the business.
does not have enough experience managing people.
q.r: Does not have enough money to operate the business. Capital is the money and other resources needed to start and run a business. Many new businesses fail because their owners underestimate start-up and operating costs and run out of money before the business becomes profitable. Too few employees, too few products, and a lack of management experience can also cause problems for a new business, but none of these is what insufficient capital means.
w: Having too few employees can cause problems, but insufficient capital specifically means not having enough money to run the business.
A small product line may hurt sales, but capital refers to the money needed to operate, not how many products a business offers.
Lack of management experience can cause a business to fail, but it is a different problem from not having enough money.

q.s: Before buying a new phone case, Lucas briefly compares the prices and colors offered at two nearby stores. Lucas is making a(n) __________ decision.
q.r: Limited. A limited decision requires some time and thought but not a great deal of research, because the decision is moderately important. Briefly comparing a few options before buying a phone case fits this description. Routine decisions are made quickly and almost automatically, such as buying a usual snack. Extensive decisions, such as choosing a college or hiring a manager, require much time and information. An impulse decision is made on the spot without planning.
w: A routine decision is made almost automatically with no comparing, such as grabbing a usual snack, while Lucas takes time to compare two stores.
An extensive decision involves lots of research and time for something important, like choosing a college, which is more than a quick phone-case comparison.
An impulse decision happens on the spot without planning, but Lucas deliberately compares prices and colors before he buys.

q.s: What is the first step in the decision-making process?
o: Evaluate the results of the decision
q.r: Define the problem or goal. The decision-making process begins by clearly defining the problem to be solved or the goal to be reached. Without a clear objective, a decision maker cannot tell which alternatives or information are relevant. Next, the decision maker identifies alternatives, gathers information, evaluates the alternatives against criteria, chooses one, acts on it, and evaluates the results. Gathering information, choosing, and evaluating results all come later in the process.
w: Gathering information is important, but it comes after defining the problem, because you need to know what you are deciding before you know what to research.
Choosing the best alternative happens near the end of the process, after the problem is defined and the options are compared.
Evaluating the results is the last step, since there are no results to check until a decision has been made and carried out.

q.s: Why is it helpful to write your personal goals down?
o: Written goals can be reached without deadlines
Written goals rarely need to be reviewed or revised
Written goals help you stay focused and track progress
Written goals take the place of an action plan
q.r: Written goals help you stay focused and track progress. Writing goals down makes them concrete and gives you something to review regularly, which keeps you focused and motivated and lets you measure your progress. Written goals still need deadlines and an action plan with specific steps and resources; they do not replace that plan. Goals should also be reviewed and revised regularly as your circumstances change.
w: Writing a goal down does not remove the need for a deadline; a written goal still needs a target date to stay on track.
Written goals still need regular review and revision as your situation changes; writing them down is what makes reviewing them easy.
A written goal says what you want to achieve, but you still need an action plan listing the specific steps to get there.

q.s: Jordan, a high school junior, has written down several personal goals. Which of his goals is a short-term goal?
o: Owning a home within the next ten years
Retiring from full-time work by age 55
Earning a B or better on Friday's test
q.r: Earning a B or better on Friday's test. A short-term goal is one that can be achieved in a relatively short time, generally a year or less. Earning a certain grade on this week's test is a specific, near-term target. Becoming a certified public accountant, owning a home in ten years, and retiring at 55 are long-term goals because they require several years of planned effort. Short-term goals often serve as milestones toward long-term goals.
w: Becoming a certified public accountant takes years of college and work experience, which makes it a long-term goal.
Owning a home within ten years stretches far beyond a year, so it is a long-term goal rather than a short-term one.
Retiring by age 55 is decades away for a high school junior, which makes it a long-term goal.

q.pt: Explain the need for innovation skills
q.s: An earbud manufacturer designs a new model with longer battery life and a built-in language translator. This is an example of __________ innovation.
q.r: Product. Product innovation is creating a new good or service or improving an existing one. Adding longer battery life and a translation feature changes what the earbuds offer customers. Process innovation changes the way a product is made or delivered, such as using faster production equipment. Paradigm innovation changes how a business or society thinks about a product or industry. Position innovation changes the context in which a product is presented, such as targeting a new market.
w: Process innovation changes how a product is made or delivered, while this company changed the earbuds themselves by adding new features.
Paradigm innovation changes the way a business or society thinks about a product or industry, not adding features to a single model.
Position innovation changes how or to whom a product is presented, such as a new target market, rather than improving the product itself.

q.pt: Explain the need for innovation skills
q.s: Why do businesses need employees who have innovation skills?
o: To help the business adapt and compete in a changing marketplace
To keep the business's processes the same over time
To reduce the need for the business to gather customer feedback
To reduce the business's need for long-range planning
q.r: To help the business adapt and compete in a changing marketplace. Innovation is turning new or improved ideas into products, processes, or services that add value. Customer needs, technology, and competition change constantly, so businesses rely on innovative employees to solve problems, improve efficiency, and develop offerings that provide a competitive advantage. Innovation brings change rather than keeping processes the same, it depends on customer feedback, and it supports rather than replaces long-range planning.
w: Keeping processes the same over time is the opposite of innovation, which is about bringing in new and improved ideas.
Innovation actually depends on customer feedback to find out what people need, so it does not reduce the need to gather it.
Innovation supports long-range planning by helping a business prepare for change; it does not replace the need to plan ahead.

q.s: Tamsin, a cashier at a grocery store, is concerned about the way weekend shifts are assigned. According to the chain of command, whom should Tamsin speak with first?
o: The owner of the grocery chain
q.r: Her immediate supervisor. The chain of command is the line of authority showing who reports to whom in an organization. Following it means taking questions and concerns to your immediate supervisor first, because that person is responsible for your work and may be able to resolve the issue. Going over a supervisor's head to the district manager or owner bypasses the chain of command and can damage working relationships. A coworker in another department has no authority over Tamsin's schedule.
w: Going straight to the district manager skips over Tamsin's own supervisor, which bypasses the chain of command and can hurt working relationships.
The owner sits at the very top of the organization, so going to the owner first would skip every level of the chain of command.
A coworker in another department has no authority over Tamsin's shifts, so talking to that person cannot resolve her concern.

q.s: What is a primary benefit of a chain of command to a business's employees?
o: It lets employees take problems directly to top management
It reduces the number of supervisors a business needs
It limits how often supervisors talk with employees
It shows employees where they fit and whom they report to
q.r: It shows employees where they fit and whom they report to. A chain of command defines the reporting relationships in an organization, often shown on an organizational chart. It helps employees understand their place in the hierarchy, whom to go to for instructions and help, and how information should flow, which reduces confusion and duplicated effort. It does not encourage skipping levels to reach top management, and it does not reduce the number of supervisors a business needs. Supervisors must still communicate regularly with the employees they oversee.
w: A chain of command sets up who reports to whom, which encourages going through proper levels rather than jumping straight to top management.
A chain of command defines reporting relationships, but it does not cut the number of supervisors a business needs.
A chain of command clarifies who supervises whom; it does not limit how often supervisors and their employees talk.

q.s: Customers at Lindell Hardware complain about long checkout lines on Saturdays. The manager learns that the store's scheduling software assigns too few cashiers on that day. The scheduling software problem is the
q.r: Root cause. A root cause is the underlying source of a problem. The long lines are a symptom, or visible sign, that a problem exists, but they result from the software assigning too few cashiers. Effective problem solvers look past symptoms to find and correct the root cause; otherwise, the problem keeps returning. An alternative is a possible solution, and a criterion is a standard used to judge alternatives.
w: The long Saturday lines are the symptom, the visible sign of trouble, while the software's understaffing is what is actually causing them.
An alternative is a possible solution to a problem, but the scheduling software is what is creating the problem, not a fix for it.
A criterion is a standard used to judge possible solutions, not the underlying source of the long checkout lines.

q.s: After clearly defining a problem, what should a problem solver do next?
o: Put the chosen solution into action
Gather facts and information about the problem
Evaluate how well the solution worked
Select the solution that costs the least
q.r: Gather facts and information about the problem. Problem solving is a systematic process. Once the problem is clearly defined, the problem solver gathers facts and information to understand its causes and scope and to check any assumptions. These facts are needed to develop and compare realistic alternatives. Implementing a solution and evaluating its results come later in the process. Selecting the cheapest solution before gathering facts skips the analysis needed to find the best one.
w: Putting a solution into action comes later, since you cannot choose a good solution before you understand the problem's causes.
Evaluating how well a solution worked is one of the last steps, after a solution has been chosen and actually tried.
Picking the cheapest solution right away skips the fact-gathering needed to understand the problem and compare realistic options.

q.pt: Write a follow-up letter after job interviews
q.s: What is the main purpose of a follow-up letter sent after a job interview?
o: To thank the interviewer and restate interest in the position
To ask the interviewer to raise the salary for the position
To request a full explanation of the hiring decision
To replace the resume submitted before the interview
q.r: To thank the interviewer and restate interest in the position. A follow-up letter, or thank-you letter, is a brief message sent after an interview to thank the interviewer for his or her time, restate the applicant's interest in the job, and reinforce how the applicant's qualifications fit the position. It also reminds the interviewer of the applicant. A follow-up letter is not the place to negotiate salary or demand an explanation of a decision, and it does not replace the resume.
w: A follow-up letter is a courtesy to thank the interviewer and show interest, not the place to push for a higher salary.
Asking for a full explanation of a hiring decision is out of place in a follow-up letter, which should be brief, grateful, and positive.
The resume stays on file with the employer, so a follow-up letter reinforces it rather than replacing it.

q.pt: Write a follow-up letter after job interviews
q.s: Carmen interviewed for a marketing assistant position on Tuesday morning. When should she send a follow-up letter to the interviewer?
o: After she receives a job offer
Two weeks later if she has not heard back
After she is invited to a second interview
q.r: By Wednesday, within about 24 hours. A follow-up letter should be sent promptly, ideally within 24 hours of the interview, while the applicant is fresh in the interviewer's mind and before a hiring decision is made. Applicants should send a follow-up after every interview, whether or not an offer seems likely. Waiting for an offer, waiting two weeks, or writing only after a second interview misses the chance to reinforce interest and qualifications.
w: Waiting for a job offer misses the point of a follow-up letter, which is to reinforce Carmen's interest before the hiring decision is made.
Waiting two weeks gives the interviewer time to forget Carmen and possibly make a decision before her letter arrives.
Carmen should send a follow-up after every interview, not only after being invited back for a second one.

q.s: Which of the following would be the most effective way to begin a resume statement describing a work accomplishment:
q.r: Coordinated. Action verbs are strong verbs, such as coordinated, organized, increased, and designed, that describe what an applicant accomplished. Starting resume statements with action verbs makes them concise and energetic and highlights the applicant's contributions. Phrases such as "was responsible for," "helped out with," and "duties included" are wordy and passive, and they describe assigned tasks rather than achievements.
w: "Was responsible for" is wordy and passive, describing an assigned duty instead of showing what the applicant actually accomplished.
"Helped out with" sounds casual and vague, and it downplays the applicant's role instead of stating a clear accomplishment.
"Duties included" lists tasks someone was assigned rather than results achieved, so it is weaker than opening with a strong action verb.

q.s: Mateo has finished writing his resume for a part-time job at a bank. What should he do before submitting it?
o: Proofread it carefully for spelling and grammar errors
Add a photograph of himself to the top of the page
Print it on brightly colored paper so that it stands out
Include the hourly wage he expects to be paid
q.r: Proofread it carefully for spelling and grammar errors. A resume is often an employer's first impression of an applicant, and even small spelling or grammar errors can suggest carelessness. Mateo should proofread carefully and ask someone else to review the resume before submitting it. In the United States, photographs are generally left off resumes. Brightly colored paper looks unprofessional, and pay expectations are usually discussed later in the hiring process rather than listed on a resume.
w: In the United States, photographs are generally left off resumes, so adding one would not help Mateo's application at a bank.
Brightly colored paper looks unprofessional, especially for a bank job, and it draws attention for the wrong reason.
Pay expectations are usually discussed later in the hiring process, so listing a desired wage on a resume is not appropriate.

q.pt: Adhere to company protocols and policies
q.s: A company rule requiring warehouse employees to wear safety goggles and steel-toed shoes is an example of a(n) __________ policy.
q.r: Health and safety. Health and safety policies are company rules designed to protect employees, customers, and visitors from injury or illness, such as requirements for protective equipment and procedures for handling hazards. Company policies are typically explained in the employee handbook. Compensation and benefits policies cover pay and employee benefits. Information security policies protect private business and customer data. Attendance and leave policies address punctuality, absences, and time off.
w: Compensation and benefits policies cover pay and perks like insurance, not protective gear that keeps warehouse workers from getting hurt.
Information security policies protect private business and customer data, while goggles and steel-toed shoes protect workers' bodies.
Attendance and leave policies cover being on time, absences, and time off, not the safety equipment workers must wear on the job.

q.s: Before deciding to explore careers in the finance career cluster, Teresa completed an aptitude test and an interest inventory. Why is this approach helpful?
o: It qualifies her for entry-level jobs in finance
It tells her which finance employers are hiring
It takes the place of researching finance careers
It bases her interest on objective information about herself
q.r: It bases her interest on objective information about herself. An aptitude test measures a person's natural abilities, and an interest inventory matches personal preferences to career areas. These tools give Teresa objective information, so her tentative occupational interest is realistic and suited to her strengths. A tentative interest is a starting point that may change as she learns more. Assessments do not qualify anyone for a job or show which employers are hiring, and they do not take the place of researching careers within the cluster.
w: Taking an aptitude test and an interest inventory helps Teresa understand herself, but it does not qualify her for any job.
These assessments measure Teresa's own abilities and preferences; they give no information about which finance employers are hiring.
The assessments point Teresa toward a career area, but she still needs to research specific finance careers to learn about them.

q.s: A hotel front-desk clerk tells a friend which room a well-known guest is staying in. The clerk has violated the hotel's rule of conduct concerning
q.r: Confidentiality. Confidentiality means protecting private business and customer information from people who are not authorized to have it. Rules of conduct set the behavior a business expects of employees, and sharing a guest's room number violates the guest's privacy and could put the guest's safety at risk. Such violations can lead to discipline or dismissal. Punctuality concerns arriving on time, company property rules concern equipment and supplies, and dress rules concern appearance.
w: Punctuality is about arriving on time, while the clerk's problem is sharing a guest's private room information.
Company property rules cover equipment and supplies, but the clerk gave away private guest information, not hotel property.
Dress and grooming rules cover how employees look at work, which has nothing to do with revealing where a guest is staying.

q.s: Which source provides information about the job duties, pay, education requirements, and job outlook for hundreds of U.S. occupations?
q.r: The Occupational Outlook Handbook. The Occupational Outlook Handbook, published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, is a reliable source of career information. It describes what workers in hundreds of occupations do, how much they earn, what education they need, and whether employment is expected to grow or decline. An employee handbook explains one company's policies. Classified ads list specific openings, and an organizational chart shows a business's reporting relationships.
w: An employee handbook explains one company's own policies and rules, not pay and outlook for hundreds of occupations.
Classified ads list specific job openings, but they do not give organized information on duties, education, and outlook for hundreds of careers.
An organizational chart shows who reports to whom inside one business, not career information about many occupations.

q.s: Which of the following is a recommended practice when writing a cover letter:
o: Tailor the letter to the specific job and company
Use the same letter for every job application
Repeat the resume's content word for word
Leave out any request for an interview
q.r: Tailor the letter to the specific job and company. A cover letter introduces the applicant, explains why he or she wants the specific position, and shows how his or her qualifications match the employer's needs. Tailoring the letter to the job and company, ideally addressing the hiring manager by name, shows genuine interest and effort. A generic letter suggests a lack of interest. Repeating the resume adds nothing new, and an effective cover letter ends with a call to action, such as requesting an interview.
w: Sending the same letter for every job looks generic and suggests little real interest in the specific position or company.
Copying the resume word for word wastes the letter, which should add new information about why the applicant fits this particular job.
An effective cover letter ends with a call to action, such as asking for an interview, so leaving that request out weakens it.

q.s: Odette works full time, takes evening classes, and helps care for her father. She feels exhausted, and the quality of her work is slipping. Which action would best help Odette balance her responsibilities?
o: Sleep fewer hours so that she can finish more tasks
Accept extra shifts to show dedication to her employer
Keep her current schedule and simply work harder
Prioritize her commitments and ask her employer about flextime
q.r: Prioritize her commitments and ask her employer about flextime. Work-life balance requires budgeting time and energy so that job responsibilities and personal needs both receive adequate attention. By setting priorities and asking about flextime, a schedule that lets employees vary their start and end times, Odette can reduce stress and avoid burnout. Sleeping less, accepting extra shifts, or working harder on the same schedule would increase her exhaustion and further harm her health and work quality.
w: Odette is already exhausted, and sleeping fewer hours would only add to her fatigue and make her work quality slip even further.
Accepting extra shifts would pile more work onto an already overloaded schedule, making it harder for Odette to balance her job, classes and caregiving.
Keeping the same schedule and simply working harder ignores the real problem, which is that Odette has more commitments than her time and energy allow.

q.pt: Determine the nature of organizational goals
q.s: The top managers of a regional grocery chain set a goal to become the area's leading retailer of organic foods within five years. This is an example of a(n) __________ goal.
q.r: Strategic. Strategic goals are broad, long-term targets set by top management to move the organization toward its mission and vision. Becoming the region's leading organic food retailer within five years is a broad, long-range aim for the whole company. Operational goals are short-term, specific targets for daily activities, such as stocking shelves by 7 a.m. Personal goals belong to individuals, and a five-year goal is not short-term.
w: Operational goals are short-term targets for daily work, such as stocking shelves by 7 a.m., not a five-year aim for the whole chain.
Personal goals belong to individuals, while this goal was set by top managers for the entire organization.
A goal set to be reached within five years is long-term, not short-term, and it covers the direction of the whole company.

q.pt: Ascertain employee's role in meeting organizational goals
q.s: Kai's company has set a goal of improving customer retention this year. Which action by Kai, a customer service representative, would best contribute to that goal?
o: Following up with customers to confirm their problems were solved
Ending calls quickly so that he can handle more calls each hour
Limiting his work to tasks listed in his original job description
Waiting for his manager to explain how his job relates to the goal
q.r: Following up with customers to confirm their problems were solved. Employees help meet organizational goals by understanding the goals and connecting their daily tasks to them, which is called alignment. Following up with customers builds satisfaction and loyalty, which directly supports customer retention. Rushing calls may leave problems unsolved and drive customers away. Limiting work to an old job description or waiting for instructions shows a lack of accountability and initiative toward the company's goals.
w: Ending calls quickly may let Kai handle more calls, but customers whose problems go unsolved are more likely to leave, which hurts retention.
Sticking only to an old job description ignores the company's new goal, and Kai can help retention by doing more to keep customers satisfied.
Waiting for a manager to explain the goal shows a lack of initiative, while Kai could already act to help keep customers.

q.s: During a meeting, a marketing team lists as many slogan ideas as possible for a new product, agreeing not to criticize any idea until the list is complete. The team is using
q.r: Brainstorming. Brainstorming is a creative technique in which a group generates as many ideas as possible in a short time, withholding judgment so people feel free to share unusual ideas. It is a form of divergent thinking. Convergent thinking narrows ideas down to the single best option, which happens after brainstorming. Benchmarking compares a business's practices to those of industry leaders. Groupthink occurs when members go along with the group to avoid conflict.
w: Convergent thinking narrows ideas down to the single best one, which would happen after the team finishes listing slogans without criticism.
Benchmarking compares a business's practices with those of industry leaders, not generating a long list of new slogan ideas in a meeting.
Groupthink is going along with the group to avoid conflict, while this team is openly sharing many different ideas without judging them.

q.s: A restaurant's manager asks employees for ideas to attract more weekday diners. Which employee suggestion shows appropriate creativity?
o: Redesigning the restaurant's logo without asking for approval
Skipping a food-safety step so that meals are served faster
Posting jokes online that mock competitors' food
Offering a low-cost weekday special that fits the restaurant's brand
q.r: Offering a low-cost weekday special that fits the restaurant's brand. Appropriate creativity means generating original, useful ideas that fit the company's goals, budget, brand, ethics, and the situation at hand. A low-cost weekday special that matches the brand meets all of these conditions. Changing the logo without approval ignores the manager's authority and brand standards. Skipping a food-safety step is unsafe and violates policy, and mocking competitors online is unprofessional and could damage the restaurant's reputation.
w: Changing the logo without approval ignores the manager's authority and the restaurant's brand standards, even if the idea is creative.
Skipping a food-safety step is unsafe and against policy, so serving meals faster this way is not an appropriate idea.
Mocking competitors online is unprofessional and could hurt the restaurant's reputation instead of attracting new diners.

q.s: Antoine must finish a sales report due tomorrow, answer several routine emails, and reorganize his supply cabinet. What should Antoine do first to manage his time effectively?
o: Rank his tasks by importance and deadline
Start with the task that is easiest to complete
Reorganize the cabinet so that he can focus
Answer each email the moment it arrives
q.r: Rank his tasks by importance and deadline. Prioritizing, or ranking tasks in order of importance and urgency, is a key time-management skill. It ensures that the most important work, such as Antoine's report due tomorrow, gets done first. Starting with the easiest task or reorganizing the cabinet can become a form of procrastination. Answering every email the moment it arrives interrupts focused work and turns email into a time waster.
w: Starting with the easiest task may feel productive, but it can delay the sales report due tomorrow, which is Antoine's most important deadline.
Reorganizing the supply cabinet is the least urgent task, so doing it first could become procrastination while the sales report waits.
Answering each email the moment it arrives keeps interrupting focused work and lets routine messages crowd out the report due tomorrow.

q.s: Store manager Lucia assigns the monthly inventory count to her assistant manager and gives him the authority to adjust work schedules as needed to finish it. Lucia is
q.r: Delegating. Delegation is assigning tasks to others along with the authority needed to complete them. It frees managers to spend their time on higher-priority responsibilities and helps develop employees' skills. Procrastinating is putting off tasks that should be done now. Micromanaging is closely controlling every detail of others' work, which is the opposite of granting authority. Multitasking is attempting to do several tasks at the same time.
w: Procrastinating means putting off tasks that should be done now, while Lucia is handing the task to someone else along with the authority to finish it.
Micromanaging means controlling every detail of someone's work, which is the opposite of giving the assistant manager authority to adjust schedules.
Multitasking means doing several tasks at the same time yourself, while Lucia is assigning the count to her assistant manager.

q.pt: Use networking techniques to identify employment opportunities
q.s: Tobias's former soccer coach tells a local business owner who is hiring that Tobias is a hard worker who should be considered for the job. The coach has provided a(n)
q.r: Referral. A referral is a recommendation of a job seeker to an employer by someone in the job seeker's professional network. Referrals are valuable because employers trust recommendations from people they know, and many jobs are filled this way. An elevator pitch is a 30- to 60-second introduction a job seeker gives about himself or herself. A cold call is contact with someone the caller does not know. A job board is a website listing job openings.
w: An elevator pitch is a short introduction a job seeker gives about themselves, but here the coach spoke to the employer on Tobias's behalf.
A cold call is reaching out to someone you do not know, while the coach is recommending Tobias to a business owner as someone worth hiring.
A job board is a website that lists job openings, not a person telling an employer that a job seeker deserves consideration.

q.pt: Identify skills needed to enhance career progression
q.s: Ayana is a top-performing sales associate who wants to become a store manager. Which skills should she develop to best prepare for the promotion?
o: In-depth product knowledge and display skills
Working independently and avoiding others' input
q.r: Leadership and strategic thinking. Career progression into management requires skills beyond those needed for an employee's current job. Managers must lead and motivate others, communicate effectively, and plan with long-term goals and the big picture in mind, which is strategic thinking. Register speed, cash-handling accuracy, product knowledge, and display skills improve performance as a sales associate but do not prepare her to manage a store. Managers must work closely with others rather than avoid their input.
w: Register speed and cash accuracy help Ayana in her current sales job, but managing a store requires leading people and planning for the long term.
Product knowledge and display skills do make Ayana a stronger sales associate, but a store manager must lead a team and think strategically about the whole store.
Managers must work closely with others and value their input, so working alone and ignoring others' ideas would hurt Ayana's chances of promotion.

q.pt: Utilize resources that can contribute to professional development (e.g., trade journals/periodicals, professional/trade associations, classes/seminars, trade shows, and mentors)
q.s: Which of the following is an activity that professional and trade associations commonly perform for their members:
o: Setting the prices that member businesses must charge
Paying the salaries of members' employees
Hiring workers on behalf of member businesses
Lobbying government officials on issues affecting the industry
q.r: Lobbying government officials on issues affecting the industry. Professional and trade associations are organizations of people or businesses in the same field. They support members by lobbying, or trying to influence legislation that affects the industry, and by offering publications, conferences, training, and networking opportunities. Associations cannot set prices for members, because agreements among competitors to fix prices are illegal under U.S. antitrust laws. Associations do not pay or hire members' employees.
w: Competitors agreeing on prices is illegal under antitrust laws, so a trade association cannot set the prices its member businesses charge.
Trade associations are funded by member dues and do not pay the salaries of members' employees; each business pays its own workers.
Member businesses do their own hiring, and associations support them with training, events and networking rather than hiring workers for them.

q.pt: Utilize resources that can contribute to professional development (e.g., trade journals/periodicals, professional/trade associations, classes/seminars, trade shows, and mentors)
q.s: Imani, a new marketing coordinator, meets monthly with a senior executive from another department who offers career advice and feedback on her goals. The executive is serving as Imani's
q.r: Mentor. A mentor is an experienced person who voluntarily guides a less experienced worker by sharing advice, knowledge, and feedback. Mentors are a valuable professional development resource because they help workers build skills, set goals, and expand their professional networks. Because the executive works in another department, he or she is not Imani's immediate supervisor. A union representative speaks for workers in labor matters, and a recruiter helps employers find job candidates.
w: The executive works in another department, so this person is not Imani's immediate supervisor who directs her daily work.
A union representative speaks for workers in labor matters, not someone who meets with Imani to give career advice.
A recruiter helps employers find job candidates, while this executive is guiding Imani's growth in the job she already has.

k.d: A business owned and operated by one person who keeps all profits and is personally responsible for all debts.
A business co-owned by two or more people who share its management and profits and, in the general form, unlimited liability for its debts.
A co-owned business in which at least one owner invests money but takes no part in management and risks only that investment.
A business that is a legal entity separate from its owners, the shareholders, whose liability is limited to the amount they invest.
The intent or purpose behind a rule, which a person honors even when its exact wording would allow otherwise.
The planning, acquiring, developing, rewarding and retaining of a company's employees so the workforce helps the business reach its goals.
The HR activity of determining the need for employees, then recruiting, selecting and hiring people to fill jobs.
Following the laws and regulations that apply to a business, such as minimum-wage, safety and antidiscrimination laws.
The introduction of a new employee to the company, the job, coworkers and policies, usually beginning on the first day.
